title: For the self or the environment? Customer mistreatment and pro-environmental behavior
abstract_text: Despite a wide investigation on the antecedents of pro-environmental behavior (PEB), factors in employee–customer interactions are poorly understood. This research, drawing from self-concept theory, theorizes that customer mistreatment impairs employees’ state self-concept (i.e., work meaningfulness), which results in decreased PEB. Moreover, employees’ trait self-concepts, i.e., self-orientation and environment-orientation, moderate the main effects. In particular, employees’ self-orientation strengthens customer mistreatment’s negative effect on work meaningfulness and subsequent PEB, while their environment-orientation protects such an effect and even reduces the negative effects of self-orientation. All our hypotheses were confirmed across a ten-day consecutive daily diary research and an experiment. This research not only enriches the antecedents and underlying mechanisms of PEB but also provides effective guidance for fostering employees’ PEB.

title: An employee lens on the dark and bright sides of customer dissatisfaction
abstract_text: Purpose Customer dissatisfaction has long been studied in the hospitality marketing literature for its powerful impacts on customer outcomes, but it has rarely been examined from the perspective of hospitality employees. Drawing on the theory of workplace anxiety, this research aims to explore how perceived customer dissatisfaction impacts employees’ emotional state of anxiety and subsequent behavioral responses, and how perceived leader empowerment functions as a motivational contingency that shapes these responses. Design/methodology/approach Study 1 employed an experimental causal-chain approach using a recall paradigm to support causal relationships between perceived customer dissatisfaction and two behaviors through workplace anxiety. In Study 2, an experience sampling methodology design with U.S. hospitality frontline employees was conducted via CloudResearch. Findings Perceived customer dissatisfaction increases employees’ workplace anxiety, which in turn, leads to voice behavior. Moreover, employees who perceive higher leader empowerment are less likely to withdraw when experiencing workplace anxiety. Practical implications Organizations can turn customer dissatisfaction into opportunities for learning and improvement by recognizing workplace anxiety as a motivator for positive behavior and by empowering employees to manage their emotions and respond proactively. Such practices can help build a more resilient, adaptive and productive workforce. Originality/value This research shifts customer dissatisfaction from a customer-focused to an employee-focused perspective. Customer dissatisfaction can be perceived as a high job demand that triggers employees’ workplace anxiety and results in divergent behavioral responses, namely, voice and withdrawal, contingent on leader empowerment.

title: Impaired control in real-life settings of gaming disorder and problematic pornography use
abstract_text: Computerspielstörung (CS) und Pornografie-Nutzungs-Störung (PNS) sind beides potenzielle Störungsbilder, die im Kontext der Verhaltensabhängigkeiten konzeptualisiert werden können. Sowohl CS als auch PNS sind charakterisiert durch eine verringerte Kontrolle über das Verhalten, eine zunehmende Priorisierung des Verhaltens, und eine Fortführung des Verhaltens trotz resultierender negativer Konsequenzen. Die verringerte Kontrolle über die jeweilige Verhaltensausführung wird als eines der zentralsten Symptome von Verhaltensabhängigkeiten betrachtet. Auf der Verhaltensebene zeigt sich verringerte Kontrolle in einzelnen konkreten Momenten der verringerten Kontrolle über die Verhaltensausführung im Alltag. Diese Konzeptualisierung scheint in der bisherigen Forschung bislang nur eine untergeordnete Rolle zu spielen. Ziel dieser kumulativen Dissertation ist es, zu untersuchen, wieso und wann solche Momente verringerter Kontrolle im Alltag von Personen mit CS und PNS auftreten. Zur Untersuchung zugrunde liegender affektiver, kognitiver und motivationaler Mechanismen realer Momente verringerter Kontrolle werden zwei theoretische Rahmenmodelle integriert, nämlich die Verhaltenssucht-Perspektive mit einem Fokus auf dem I-PACE-Modell, sowie die Selbstregulations-Perspektive mit einem Fokus auf dem PI-Modell der Selbstkontrolle. In der ersten Schrift wird bestehende Forschung zu Verhaltensabhängigkeiten im natürlichen Umfeld systematisch aufgearbeitet, um methodische Ansätze zur Untersuchung von Momenten verringerter Kontrolle zu identifizieren, sowie zentrale zugrunde liegende Mechanismen der Ausführung realen Verhaltens herauszuarbeiten. Reizreaktivität, Craving und Verstärkungsmechanismen erwiesen sich dabei als zentrale Prädiktoren der realen Verhaltensausführung, während die Befundlage zur Inhibitionskontrolle bislang begrenzt und inkonsistent erscheint. Im Rahmen der zweiten Schrift wurde das Dual-Prozess-Zusammenspiel von Reiz-Reaktivität und Craving, sowie die Reduktion der verhaltensspezifischen Inhibitionskontrolle auf Grundlage einer Labor-Erhebung und eines Ambulatory Assessments bei CS und PNS untersucht. Die Ergebnisse zeigten, dass innerhalb von Personen ein erhöhtes Craving mit einer verminderten verhaltensspezifischen Inhibitionskontrolle einherging, was ihrerseits eine erhöhte Wahrscheinlichkeit für das Auftreten eines Moments der verringerten Kontrolle vorhersagte. In der dritten Schrift wurden Craving, Regulationsmotivation und Selbstlizenzierung als zugrunde liegende Mechanismen von Momenten der verringerten Kontrolle in konflikthaften Alltagssituationen bei CS und PNS untersucht. Die Ergebnisse zeigten, dass erhöhtes Craving und stärkere Selbstlizenzierung einen nachfolgenden Moment der verringerten Kontrolle vorhersagten; Regulationsmotivation tat dies hingegen nicht. Insgesamt tragen die Befunde dieser Dissertation dazu bei, bestehende methodische Ansätze zur Untersuchung des Symptoms beeinträchtigter Kontrolle im alltäglichen, natürlichen Umfeld bei Verhaltensabhängigkeiten wie CS und PNS zu erweitern. Besonders hervorzuheben ist, dass die Erkenntnisse dieser Dissertation in einem theoretischen Rahmenmodell zugrunde liegender affektiver, kognitiver und motivationaler Mechanismen spezifischer Momente verringerter Kontrolle integriert werden. Dieses Rahmenmodell dient erstens als Grundlage für zukünftige Studien zu verringerter Kontrolle in realen Situationen. Zweitens ist es auch von klarer klinischer Relevanz für Prävention und Intervention, da es jene Prozesse herausstellt, die in realen Momenten verringerte Kontrolle bei Verhaltensabhängigkeiten, wie CS und PNS, besonders bedeutsam sind.

title: Behavioral and Contextual Patterns Derived From Ecological Momentary Assessment and Wearable Sensors and Their Associations With Health-Related Outcomes: WEALTH Cross-Sectional Study
abstract_text: Abstract Background Physical activity, sedentary behavior, sleep, and eating behavior are recognized as key contributors to physical and mental health. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) can capture both the temporal variations and contextual correlates of these behaviors. Objective This study aimed to identify, in adults, (1) multibehavioral clusters, including the social, physical, and psychological contexts as assessed by EMA; and (2) the associations of these behaviors with selected health-related outcomes. Methods A sample of 510 participants from Czechia, Germany, France, and Ireland, with cross-sectional data collected in 2023‐2024, was included (WEALTH study; median age 35.5, IQR 25.0-50.0 y; n=289, 56.7% female participants). During a 7-day free-living period, data on sedentary behavior (activPAL), physical activity (ActiGraph), sleep, eating behavior, and contextual characteristics (EMA) were collected. Dietary intake (Food Frequency Questionnaire) was assessed prior to the 7-day period. We used factor analysis of mixed data on 35 variables and then applied hierarchical clustering on principal components. Linear regression models with robust variance were used to examine associations between the clusters and health-related quality of life (36-Item Short Form Health Survey), well-being (5-item World Health Organization Well-Being Index), and handgrip strength. A multinomial logistic regression was used to examine the association between clusters and self-rated health. Results Four multibehavioral clusters were identified: unhealthy behavior (n=109, reference group), mixed behavior–healthy diet (n=173), mixed behavior–stable good mood (n=142), and healthy behavior (n=86). The mixed behavior–stable good mood and healthy behavior clusters showed significantly higher average scores on mental health-related quality of life (β=6.32, 95% CI 3.73‐8.91 and β=5.61, 95% CI 2.47‐8.75, respectively) and well-being (β=11.62, 95% CI 7.86‐15.38 and β=9.63, 95% CI 5.17‐14.10, respectively) compared with the unhealthy behavior cluster. Participants in these clusters and those in the mixed behavior–healthy diet cluster tended to report better perceived health than those in the unhealthy behavior cluster (odds ratio [OR] 3.19, 95% CI 1.20‐8.49; OR 9.85, 95% CI 3.54‐27.40; OR 12.18, 95% CI 4.04‐36.71, respectively). Conclusions These findings indicate that engaging in multiple healthy lifestyle behaviors is associated with better health outcomes than focusing on a single domain and demonstrate the opportunity to identify meaningful multibehavioral patterns related to health by using EMA combined with body-worn movement sensors.

title: Why we should be using real world data to improve pharmacotherapy in psychiatry
abstract_text: Psychiatric pharmacotherapy is often effective for patients. For example, symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are typically ameliorated by stimulant medications. However, identifying the best medication for an individual or their optimal dose can be difficult because clinical visits and retrospective symptom reports only capture snapshots of the underlying dynamic, context-dependent treatment trajectories. Real-world data approaches, obtained from smartphones and wearable technologies, can potentially provide a rich source of information for individual optimization of pharmacotherapy, yet they are infrequently used. First, these tools enable remote, high-frequency monitoring of medication efficacy and side effects, tracking core symptoms plus comorbid psychopathology, sleep, and autonomic function throughout titration. Second, densely sampled cognitive task data and ecological momentary assessment offer a route to understanding changes to neurocognitive mechanisms in response to medication. Third, real-world data can help redress the persistent sex disparities in pharmacotherapeutic research and practice by characterizing how symptoms and treatment response interact with sex-specific life events. We conclude with recommendations for future research and practice.

title: De keerzijde van de placenta: respiratoire klachten als eerste presentatie van een zeldzaam choriocarcinoom
abstract_text: The hidden face of the placenta: pulmonary metastasis due to choriocarcinoma Introduction: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) comprises rare tumors arising from placental trophoblastic cells. Choriocarcinoma is a potentially life-threatening form of GTN but generally carries an excellent prognosis due to high chemosensitivity. Although pulmonary metastases are common, presentation with respiratory symptoms is rare and may cause diagnostic delay. Case: A 32-year-old woman, G1P0, with a history of a non-viable pregnancy treated with misoprostol and curettage, presented with chest pain and hemoptysis. Laboratory analysis showed an hCG level of 271 320 IU/L. Chest CT revealed bilateral centrilobular pulmonary nodules. FDG-PET/CT and pelvic MRI confirmed a large uterine choriocarcinoma with lung metastases and signs of uterine perforation. The disease was classified as FIGO stage III with a WHO prognostic score of 12, indicating high-risk GTN. Treatment and course: The patient received 11 cycles of EMA-CO chemotherapy until hCG became undetectable, followed by 4 consolidation cycles. Treatment was well tolerated and resulted in complete remission with persistently undetectable hCG during follow-up. After one year of contraception, the patient underwent an ICSI program, resulting in a successful intrauterine pregnancy. Discussion: This case highlights that respiratory symptoms may be the first manifestation of choriocarcinoma. hCG measurement should be considered in women with respiratory complaints and risk factors such as a recent or possibly unrecognized pregnancy. Strict hCG monitoring for one year remains essential because of a small but real recurrence risk. Conclusion: Choriocarcinoma may present atypically with respiratory symptoms. In women with recent pregnancy and respiratory complaints, hCG testing is warranted. With appropriate imaging, staging and treatment, the prognosis is excellent, even in metastatic disease.

title: Effects of a Smartphone-Based Mindfulness Intervention on Momentary Stress Among First Responders: a Micro-Randomized Trial
abstract_text: First responders face extreme workplace stressors that can increase symptoms of distress. While mindfulness-based interventions are well-established for stress management, their time-intensive formats may pose barriers for those with long shifts and unpredictable schedules. Smartphone-delivered mindfulness interventions offer a flexible alternative. This study used a micro-randomized controlled trial design to test the effectiveness of two smartphone-delivered mindfulness interventions in reducing momentary stress and stress reactivity to a self-reported stressor. The two interventions included: (1) a text message reminder to engage in a mindfulness practice (brief message) and (2) a prompt to complete an app-based guided mindfulness practice (MYAPT.MIND). Participants were 75 first responders (M = 38.9, SD = 6.8) who completed ecological momentary assessments twice a day (EMA 1 and EMA 2) and received 1 of 3 conditions daily (i.e., no-intervention, brief message, or MYAPT.MIND) between EMA 1 and EMA 2 for 30 days. Multilevel modeling was used to estimate the proximal effects of the daily intervention assignments and to test whether the interventions dampened the impact of stressor exposures on momentary stress at EMA 2. Results indicated no direct effect of interventions on momentary stress. However, participants who were assigned to MYAPT.MIND reported smaller increases in momentary stress following a stressor exposure than for the brief message or control groups. These findings highlight the potential of app-based mindfulness interventions as a "just-in-time" tool for acute stress management.

title: Trapped in thought: Investigating reciprocal links between negative interpretation inflexibility, rumination, and dampening of positive emotions in daily life.
abstract_text: Rumination and dampening of positive emotions are consistently linked to poor mental health outcomes, yet the mechanisms underlying these repetitive thinking patterns remain underspecified. One candidate mechanism is negative interpretation inflexibility (persistence of negative interpretations of ambiguous situations over time). However, little is known about how these processes unfold in everyday life. Addressing this gap, the present study examined whether momentary negative interpretation inflexibility predicts subsequent rumination and dampening in daily life, and whether these repetitive thought patterns in turn predict the persistence of negative interpretations. A community sample of 179 adults with varying depression and social anxiety levels completed a 14-day ecological momentary assessment protocol (12,950 completed surveys). Ecological momentary assessment prompts included a novel mobile cognitive task (the Daily Life Interpretation Inflexibility Task) to assess the persistence of negative interpretations, alongside self-report measures of rumination and dampening. Preregistered multilevel analyses showed that within-person increases in negative interpretation inflexibility predicted subsequent increases in rumination and dampening. In the reverse direction, rumination, but not dampening, predicted subsequent increases in negative interpretation inflexibility. These temporal relations were not moderated by depression or social anxiety. Complementary dynamic structural equation models revealed significant reciprocal cross-lagged effects between negative interpretation inflexibility and rumination, and small reciprocal cross-lagged effects with dampening. These findings highlight negative interpretation inflexibility as a dynamic process that both precedes and follows repetitive thinking patterns in daily life. This work highlights negative interpretation persistence as a potential target for ecological interventions to reduce harmful repetitive thought. title: Dynamic latent class structural equation modeling: A hands-on tutorial for modeling intensive longitudinal data.
abstract_text: In this tutorial, we provide a hands-on guideline on how to implement complex dynamic latent class structural equation models (DLCSEMs) in the Bayesian software JAGS. We provide building blocks starting with simple confirmatory factor and time-series analysis and then extend these blocks to multilevel models and dynamic structural equation models. Subsequently, we introduce hidden Markov switching models and demonstrate their integration with dynamic structural equation models to yield DLCSEM. Leading through the tutorial is an example from clinical psychology using data on a generalized anxiety treatment that includes scales on anxiety symptoms and the Working Alliance Inventory, which measures the alliance between therapists and patients. Within each block, we provide an overview, specific hypotheses we want to test, the resulting model and its implementation, and an interpretation of the results. The aim of this tutorial is to provide a step-by-step guide for applied researchers that enables them to use this flexible DLCSEM framework for their own analyses. title: Within‐Person Relationships between Adolescents’ Daily Election Exposure, Negative Election‐Related Emotions, and Motivation to Address Social Justice Issues
abstract_text: ABSTRACT Election‐related emotions, particularly negative emotions, are one factor that can shape and be shaped by motivation to engage with social change. Negative emotions (i.e., anger, fear, anxiety, disgust, sadness, embarrassment, and guilt) can serve as a catalyst for engaging in social change. This daily diary study explored associations between adolescents’ daily experiences of negative election‐related emotions, election‐related exposure, and motivation to address social justice issues (i.e., racism/discrimination and social/economic inequalities). Over the course of three weeks, throughout the 2024 U.S. Election, thirty‐six adolescents aged 13–18 living in the swing state of North Carolina who mostly identified as White, female, and Democratic ( M = 15.61, SD = 1.23) reported 445 daily observations. Multilevel models in which days (Level 1) were nested within people (Level 2) revealed that participants’ motivation to address social justice issues and negative election‐related emotions fluctuated significantly from day to day. Further, participants tended to report more negative election‐related emotions on days with higher election‐related exposure. On days with higher negative election‐related emotions, participants tended to report enhanced motivation to address racism. However, effects were small, indicating that there is still much to explore regarding the factors that predict daily fluctuations in adolescent motivation to address social justice issues, especially in a polarized political world.

title: Daily Ageism, Subjective Age, and Memory Failures: A Multi-Country Integrated Data Analysis
abstract_text: Memory functioning is central to everyday life, yet memory failures, such as forgetting names, words, or medications, are common daily experiences, particularly in later adulthood. How often individuals experience these memory failures may depend on their general and personal views of aging. General views include expectations for older adults (ageist attitudes), whereas personal views can include age-based experiences of discrimination (ageist experiences) and subjective age. Leveraging 14-day daily diary data from 974 participants (aged 50–94 years) who reported on a total of 12,261 days from the United States, Canada, Germany, Austria, Ukraine, India, China, Israel, and Türkiye (Study 1), and momentary data across 14 days with 7 assessments per day from 111 participants (aged 65–91 years) from Switzerland (Study 2), the current studies examined within-person fluctuations in daily ageism and daily subjective age and their links to everyday self-reported memory failures. Preregistered analyses tested between- and within-person effects of subjective age and ageism (ageist attitudes in Study 1, ageist experiences in Study 2) in predicting daily memory failures. Study 1 results indicate that within- and between-person ageist attitudes were positively associated with daily memory failures, but subjective age was not. Study 2 results from the Swiss data revealed no significant associations. title: Intra-day Coupling of Emotional Dynamics, Self-regulation, and Loss of Control Over Eating Among Women During Fat Loss: A 7-Day Ecological Momentary Assessment Study
abstract_text: This study employs ecological momentary assessment (EMA) to examine the dynamic relationships among affect, self-regulatory states, and loss-of-control eating in naturalistic daily-life contexts. To address these limitations, the present study uses intensive repeated measurements to test whether momentary deviations in affect and self-regulation from an individual’s usual levels are associated with concurrent or subsequent loss-of-control eating. Participants will first complete baseline questionnaires assessing demographic and physical characteristics, eating-disorder risk, depressive symptoms, and trait self-control. They will then complete six EMA assessments per day for seven consecutive days, yielding a planned maximum of 42 reports per participant. At each assessment, participants will report their momentary positive affect, negative affect, loss-of-control eating-related cognitions, and self-regulatory difficulties, as well as whether loss-of-control eating has occurred since the previous assessment. Information on sleep, physical activity, and participant-reported potential triggers will also be collected. The study primarily addresses three questions. First, are momentary affect and self-regulatory difficulties associated with loss-of-control eating within the same assessment interval? Second, can affective and self-regulatory states at one time point predict newly occurring loss-of-control eating at the subsequent time point? Third, following an episode of loss-of-control eating, do participants’ subsequent affective or self-regulatory states change? Analyses will distinguish within-person effects from between-person effects and will use multilevel generalized linear mixed models to account for the hierarchical structure of EMA observations nested within participants. title: Evidence on the validity, reliability and usability of active and passive sensing of cognition for use in ambulatory studies: A systematic scoping review
abstract_text: Cognitive functions are traditionally measured as trait-like constructs in highly controlled lab settings using paper-based or computerized tasks. Growing emphasis on ecological validity and the increasing use of ecological momentary assessment (EMA) have shifted research focus towards repeated or continuous assessment of cognitive states in daily life. Usability outcomes were generally positive across studies but less frequently investigated than validity and reliability. title: Examining the use of experience sampling methods in sport psychology research: a scoping review
abstract_text: Introduction Experience sampling methods (ESMs) allow researchers to capture the variability in momentary human experiences by collecting repeated self-report measures within or across days. Real-time fluctuations in psychological processes, which are commonly distorted by retrospective bias in traditional survey designs, can be more accurately recorded using this approach. Results The search yielded 1,474 studies, of which 73 were included. The included studies primarily focused on the experiences of sport participants, with limited representation of coaches, parents, or spectators. Discussion Given the limited use of ESMs and narrow focus on specific contexts, designs, and topics, continued investigation is warranted to better understand critical momentary experiences in sport.

title: Evidence on the validity, reliability and usability of active and passive sensing of cognition for use in ambulatory studies: A systematic scoping review
abstract_text: Cognitive functions are traditionally measured as trait-like constructs in highly controlled lab settings using paper-based or computerized tasks. Growing emphasis on ecological validity and the increasing use of ecological momentary assessment (EMA) have shifted research focus towards repeated or continuous assessment of cognitive states in daily life. This includes cognitive tasks or questions delivered via mobile devices (active sensing), and objective indicators such as keystroke dynamics derived from smartphone sensors (passive sensing). However, the psychometric properties and usability of these approaches have not yet been established systematically. This scoping review evaluated the evidence on validity, reliability and usability of cognitive assessments for use in ambulatory research. In total, 88 studies were included, with most examining active cognitive sensing (n = 72) and fewer studies on passive sensing (n = 13) or both (n = 3). Among active cognitive assessments, processing speed tasks demonstrated the most consistent and robust psychometric evidence on mobile devices relative to other cognitive domains. Keystroke dynamics, among other passive sensing features, showed consistent initial associations with processing speed measures, and some evidence to distinguish between clinical and non-clinical groups. Despite these promising findings, only a few studies explicitly assessed between- and within-person reliability within EMA settings. Usability outcomes were generally positive across studies but less frequently investigated than validity and reliability. Future research should develop and adopt standardized approaches to evaluate mobile-based cognitive assessments. Eventually such measures will enable research on cognitive fluctuations and their dynamic relationships with stress, behavior and health in real-world contexts.

title: Daily life stress measurement strategies: A scoping review
abstract_text:
Aim. This scoping review of daily momentary stress measurement studies synthesizes a booming but fragmented field of stress research and introduces the stress MEasurement StrategieS (StressMess) database.
Methods. Systematic searches in Web of Science, MEDLINE, and PsycINFO identified studies of (a) stress and psychopathology (e.g., anxiety/depression) using (b) time series or ambulatory assessment designs where (c) stress was measured at least daily on two consecutive days. 
Results. We identified 12,846 articles and included 721 studies into the StressMess database, of which half in the past five years, typically with larger samples and more frequent measurements than older studies. Most participants were young adults (aged 18-24, M=67% women), from general populations in the US (55%), Germany (7%), and the Netherlands (5%). Stress was often operationalized as a stressor (27%) or stress response to adverse events (33%), and measured as characteristics of events (e.g., type, frequency, predictability, stressfulness, unpleasantness), or general momentaneous or daily stress score (27%), or as stress response via emotions (5%), or physiology (<1%). Some studies (13%) used multiple stress operationalizations. 
Conclusion. Stress is currently not a useful scientific concept because of the large heterogeneity in definitions, terminology, measurement strategies (instruments), and study design. We provide directions to improve conceptualizations and design for future studies focusing on measuring stress. The StressMess database is open source (www.stressmess.nl) to improve the understanding, prevention, and treatment of adverse (mental) health effects of stress. Stress measurement influences what stress research can identify and thereby clinical practice.

title: A recipe for an ESM study: An illustrative example of a comprehensive design
abstract_text: Despite their wide application, designing Experience Sampling Method (ESM) studies remains challenging partly due to complex and interdependent methodological decisions, such as sampling schedules, response formats, and technological platforms. The existing literature provides valuable frameworks but often mentions methodological options without concrete examples; this article aims to bridge this gap in practical guidance. Informed by the existing ESM literature, we illustrate our decision-making process while designing an ESM study on the temporal associations between momentary life meaning, eating disorder symptoms, and negative affect. While grounded in our specific research questions, this paper provides practical guidelines on how to decide among various methodological options for researchers across psychological fields. We outline key decisions, practical considerations, and challenges encountered during the study’s development. Our paper provides a practical checklist to support researchers in designing ESM studies from scratch and in reporting essential aspects in their manuscripts, promoting transparency and replicability. By illustrating a real-life example of setting up our own study, we aim to guide researchers in navigating the complexities of ESM design.

title: Trait and State Emotional Granularity: Personality Correlates and Momentary Dynamics in Adolescents
abstract_text: This study investigates emotional granularity (EG) — the ability to differentiate discrete emotional states — separately for positive (PEG) and negative (NEG) affect, and at two levels of analysis: trait (a single person-level aggregate across the study period) and state (momentary, EMA-derived fluctuations within a person over time). The purpose is twofold: first, to test established and theory-driven predictions about how trait EG relates to personality; second, to extend EG research into the state level and explore the construct of state emotional granularity, which remains largely unexplored in the literature. At the trait level, the study examines Big Five personality correlates of EG. It directly replicates and extends prior work (Erbas et al., 2014) by testing whether trait negative EG is positively associated with ego resilience and negatively associated with neuroticism, now using a richer EMA-derived measure rather than a small fixed set of emotion terms. It also explores, on a more tentative basis, whether trait positive EG relates to ego resilience, openness to experience, and neuroticism, drawing on broaden-and-build theory. A further exploratory aim examines how trait EG (both valences) relates to affect dynamics indices such as emotional instability and inertia, to map how EG sits relative to other measures of emotional patterning. At the state level, the study tests whether having a test — treated as an ecologically valid acute stressor for adolescents — predicts lower momentary negative EG on that day, extending prior daily-diary findings to a within-person, day-level test. Beyond this, the study explores the temporal stability of state EG (via mean square successive difference and autocorrelation) and examines whether positive and negative EG behave as distinct constructs at the momentary level, comparing their trends over time and their within-person correlation. A key preliminary observation motivating this last analysis is that the person-specific correlation between momentary positive and negative EG varies across individuals, suggesting that a single population-level PEG–NEG relationship may not adequately describe individual experience. Expected outcomes include: (1) confirmatory evidence on whether trait negative EG relates to ego resilience and neuroticism as predicted, addressing a previously marginal replication; (2) exploratory evidence on trait positive EG's personality correlates; and (3) new descriptive findings on how EG behaves as a fluctuating state-level construct, including its stability over time and the individual variability in how positive and negative EG relate to one another within a person. Because state-level EG research is nascent, the state-level findings are intended primarily to generate hypotheses and inform the design of future confirmatory studies, including potential follow-up work treating individual differences in PEG–NEG within-person correlations as an outcome predicted by trait variables such as psychopathology status, neuroticism, or mindfulness.

title: Which Symptom Leads Depends on the Person
abstract_text: Early identification of psychological deterioration is often framed around finding a symptom sequence that generalizes across people: if some symptoms reliably precede others, a monitoring system could flag those earlier-moving symptoms before overall state has clearly worsened. We test this framing using a public intensive longitudinal EMA dataset of 40 individuals with generalized anxiety disorder or major depressive disorder, and find it does not hold. A group-averaged lead-lag ranking across 21 symptoms suggests positive affect, worry, and tension precede others, while depressed mood lags; computed separately per individual, direction is statistically indistinguishable from chance for every symptom (binomial tests, all p &gt; .25). A noise-calibrated null model, using a moving block bootstrap to preserve temporal dependence, shows this disagreement exceeds what estimation error alone predicts for tension and depressed mood (p = .0014 and p &lt; .001, Holm-adjusted p = .0042 and p = .0012), a pattern stable across a range of block lengths, though not for positive affect or worry (p = .254 and p = .051), consistent with genuine heterogeneity in two of four symptoms rather than insufficient power at N = 40. Mood inertia, by contrast, is consistent within individuals (82.5% individually significant), showing this washout is specific to sequence, not a general failure to detect structure. We report a secondary forecasting test that is directionally suggestive but not confirmed. These findings challenge a common assumption in psychopathology research: that population-level symptom dynamics generalize to individuals. Not every apparently coherent aggregate symptom direction reflects genuine heterogeneity, but some do, and these cannot be explained by estimation noise alone.

abstract_text: Methodische Perspektiven und pharmakodynamische Überlegungen bei der Evaluierung von mRNA-LNP-Plattformen: Ein sokratisches Kompendium ungelöster pathophysiologischer offener Fragen der Vascular Pharmacodynamic and Autoimmunity Research Core Group (VPARCG) Autor: Vascular Pharmacodynamic and Autoimmunity Research Core Group (VPARCG)Digital Object Identifier (DOI): 10.5281/zenodo.21840325Schlüsselwörter: mRNA-Plattform-Pharmakokinetik, Lipid-Nanopartikel, Endothelitis, Self-Controlled Case Series, ICH-GCP-Konformität, vaskuläre Sicherheit, Simoa-Antigenpersistenz Abstract Nach fast sechs Jahren des weltweiten Einsatzes von Lipid-Nanopartikel (LNP)-verkapselten Messenger-RNA (mRNA)-Plattformen bleiben selbst für medizinische Fachkräfte, die seit Jahrzehnten in diesem Bereich tätig sind, offene Fragen bestehen – beispielsweise, ob erhebliche Lücken zwischen der Übertragung struktureller molekularer Pharmakokinetik-/Pharmakodynamik-Daten von Tier- auf Menschenmodelle und proaktiven klinischen Überwachungsmethoden bestehen, während gleichzeitig bekannt ist, dass diese Immunisierungstechnik von einer völlig anderen Art ist als die von konventionellen Impfstoffen genutzte Technologie. Diese Fragen müssen daher beantwortet werden. Neben diesen Fragestellungen skizziert dieses VPARCG-Papier 80 miteinander verknüpfte, nicht evaluierte pathophysiologische und methodische Fragen zu mRNA-Formulierungen der ersten und zweiten Generation (einschließlich COVID-19-, RSV- und saisonaler Influenza-Konstrukte [INF]). Einleitung: Die Notwendigkeit epistemischer Klarheit Die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung der modernen Medizin basiert auf einem transparenten, produktiven Dialog zwischen präklinischen Modellen, klinischer Praxis und regulatorischer Aufsicht. Nach sechs Jahren weltweiter Erfahrung mit Lipid-Nanopartikel (LNP)-verkapselten mRNA-Plattformen (einschließlich COVID-19-, RSV- und Influenza-Formulierungen) teilen Regulierungsbehörden und Gesetzgeber eine entscheidende Aufgabe: das Vertrauen der Öffentlichkeit durch die Erfassung fortgeschrittener, vom Menschen abgeleiteter Post-Marketing-Sicherheitsdaten zu stärken. Dieses Memorandum ist ausdrücklich keine Anklage gegen vergangene regulatorische Maßnahmen. Stattdessen dient es als vorgeschlagene konstruktive Ressource und wissenschaftlicher Kompass, basierend auf langjähriger klinischer Expertenmeinung. Es zielt darauf ab, eine kollaborative Brücke zu bauen (z. B. für die Vereinigten Staaten: zwischen der Food and Drug Administration (FDA/CBER) und den gesetzgebenden Ausschüssen des US-Kongresses (Senat und Repräsentantenhaus), der aktuellen Führung im Gesundheitswesen unter Robert F. Darüber hinaus ist diese Initiative als fortlaufendes, lebendes Projekt konzipiert, das in den kommenden Jahren über den Zenodo-Server des CERN unter der permanenten Concept-DOI (siehe oben) kontinuierlich aktualisiert wird. Der Eckpfeiler der evidenzbasierten Medizin beruht auf dem kontinuierlichen Abgleich präklinischer Modelle mit realen klinischen Beobachtungen. title: The Chameleon Neuron: Emergent Retention, Transmutation, and Abstention in a Continual-Learning Organism
abstract_text: We present the Chameleon Neuron, a continual-learning organism whose unit is a low-rankstem neuron with epigenetic marks and a context meta-selector, organized as a dynamicpopulation that grows by neurogenesis, specializes into niches, and consolidates offline.Rather than treating forgetting, domain adaptation and out-of-distribution (OOD) detectionas separate problems, we show that three capabilities coexist on one substrate, withoutbinary masks and without replay: retention (not forgetting), transmutation (classifyingknown-but-corrupted inputs), and abstention (rejecting true OOD). We validate onSplit-CIFAR-100 over frozen ResNet-18 features (5 seeds) and, unusually, audit our ownclaims adversarially, reporting what survives and what does not. We do not claim per-axissupremacy: retention matches PackNet at the reported size (BWT -0.00 +/- 0.16%, 85.10 +/-0.43%), but at matched parameters PackNet and EWC pull ahead, and a learned L2P-stylerouter beats our task-free routing (55.8% vs 38.6% Class-IL) with 1/26 of the parameters.One robustness result turns a principle into a method: signal decoupling. A decoupledlearned gate combining distance and energy is the only detector strong on both far- andnear-OOD (0.99 far, 0.83 SVHN), where distance collapses on near-OOD and energy is weak onfar-OOD; the contribution is insurance against regime collapse, not an accuracy win. Theaudit methodology is itself a contribution: it exposed and made us fix an abstention gatecalibrated on the test set, and routing inflated by homogeneous batches plus an EMA-scalebug (honest per-sample routing 36% -> 44.6%). Every number that survived bad faith isreported as such; every one that did not, we fixed or retired.

title: Beyond Pain Scores: A Mixed-Methods Framework for Studying Medical Cannabis Outcomes
abstract_text: Medical cannabis outcomes cannot be adequately characterized by symptom scores alone. This methodological framework proposes a longitudinal convergent mixed-methods design in which quantitative and qualitative data are collected repeatedly over the same period and intentionally integrated. Quantitative measurement emphasizes precise characterization of THC/CBD exposure, validated symptom and function measures, medication burden, adverse effects, and ecological momentary assessment. Qualitative inquiry examines the functional and personal meaning of change, treatment decisions, and experiences that conventional instruments may fail to capture. Purposeful maximum-variation and negative-case sampling are proposed to interrogate divergent outcome trajectories, while joint displays support integrated interpretation. The framework is intended to strengthen validity, reliability, trustworthiness, and clinically meaningful inference in medical cannabis research.

title: Methodological Perspectives and Pharmacodynamic Considerations in mRNA-LNP Platform Evaluation: A Socratic Compendium of Unresolved Pathophysiological Open Questions by the Vascular Pharmacodynamic and Autoimmunity Research Core Group (VPARCG)

Sie wurde unter Notfallbedingungen entwickelt, wodurch Parameter bezüglich Arzneimittelwechselwirkungen, langfristiger Karzinogenität und neuartiger Lipid-Gewebetoxizität im Rahmen der ursprünglichen Zulassung strukturell für die Post-Marketing-Evaluierung im beschleunigten Verfahren vorgesehen waren. Unter Berufung auf historische Präzedenzfälle fordert die Contergan-Lehre eine proaktive toxikologische Validierung, während das Kortikosteroid-Paradigma vor unüberwachtem, latentem Gewebeabbau warnt. Das offizielle WHO-Rahmenwerk stellt fest, dass da mRNA-LNP-Konstrukte eine völlig neue Technologieklasse darstellen, mehrere mechanistische Fragen offenbleiben, die eine kontinuierliche Datenüberwachung und proaktive Sicherheitsbewertungen rechtfertigen. Diese Fragen müssen daher beantwortet werden. Neben diesen Fragestellungen skizziert dieses VPARCG-Papier 80 miteinander verknüpfte, nicht evaluierte pathophysiologische und methodische Fragen zu mRNA-Formulierungen der ersten und zweiten Generation (einschließlich COVID-19-, RSV- und saisonaler Influenza-Konstrukte [INF]). Indem die VPARCG diese als offene wissenschaftliche Fragen formuliert, versucht sie – basierend auf drei Jahrzehnten klinischer Erfahrung in der Immunologie/Rheumatologie und klinischen Epidemiologie –, Regulierungsbehörden und Herstellern einen systematischen Fahrplan an die Hand zu geben, um durch objektive, vom Menschen abgeleitete Daten in der Post-Marketing-Phase mehr wissenschaftliche Klarheit zu erlangen. 1. Einleitung: Die Notwendigkeit epistemischer Klarheit Die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung der modernen Medizin basiert auf einem transparenten, produktiven Dialog zwischen präklinischen Modellen, klinischer Praxis und regulatorischer Aufsicht. Nach sechs Jahren weltweiter Erfahrung mit Lipid-Nanopartikel (LNP)-verkapselten mRNA-Plattformen (einschließlich COVID-19-, RSV- und Influenza-Formulierungen) teilen Regulierungsbehörden und Gesetzgeber eine entscheidende Aufgabe: das Vertrauen der Öffentlichkeit durch die Erfassung fortgeschrittener, vom Menschen abgeleiteter Post-Marketing-Sicherheitsdaten zu stärken. Dieses Memorandum ist ausdrücklich keine Anklage gegen vergangene regulatorische Maßnahmen. Stattdessen dient es als vorgeschlagene konstruktive Ressource und wissenschaftlicher Kompass, basierend auf langjähriger klinischer Expertenmeinung. Es zielt darauf ab, eine kollaborative Brücke zu bauen (z. B. für die Vereinigten Staaten: zwischen der Food and Drug Administration (FDA/CBER) und den gesetzgebenden Ausschüssen des US-Kongresses (Senat und Repräsentantenhaus), der aktuellen Führung im Gesundheitswesen unter Robert F. Kennedy Jr. und führenden Regulierungsexperten wie FDA Chefetage, sowie für alle anderen Länder). Das Ziel ist die Etablierung einer gemeinsamen Forschungsagenda, die innovative Technologien mit dem Grundprinzip des primum non nocere harmonisiert. Darüber hinaus ist diese Initiative als fortlaufendes, lebendes Projekt konzipiert, das in den kommenden Jahren über den Zenodo-Server des CERN unter der permanenten Concept-DOI (siehe oben) kontinuierlich aktualisiert wird. Der Eckpfeiler der evidenzbasierten Medizin beruht auf dem kontinuierlichen Abgleich präklinischer Modelle mit realen klinischen Beobachtungen. In den vergangenen sechs Jahren hat die rasche Übertragung der mRNA-LNP-Plattform von einer experimentellen Modalität zu einem grundlegenden Werkzeug der öffentlichen Gesundheit die Landschaft der Präventivmedizin verändert. Doch trotz umfangreicher statistischer Daten zu makrovaskulären klinischen Endpunkten bleiben mehrere zentrale mechanistische und methodische Fragen im öffentlichen Konsens und in der regulatorischen Dokumentation unberücksichtigt. Medizinische Fachkräfte sind durch die Prinzipien des primum non nocere verpflichtet, die biologische Plausibilität massenhaft angewandter Therapeutika kontinuierlich zu überprüfen. Um diesen laufenden wissenschaftlichen Dialog zu unterstützen, formalisiert dieses Memorandum einen strukturierten Katalog grundlegender Fragen zur systematischen Evaluierung und Klärung durch Regulierungsbehörden (wie die FDA und EMA) und die pharmazeutische Industrie in den kommenden Jahren. Nur durch vom Menschen abgeleitete, objektive kinetische Daten können echte wissenschaftliche Klarheit und ein robustes öffentliches Vertrauen erreicht werden. Letztlich dient dieser Rahmen dazu, die definitive Frage zu beantworten, die medizinische Fachkräfte derzeit stellen: Ist eine breite Massenanwendung dieser neu eingeführten, nicht vollständig charakterisierten Plattformtechnologie medizinisch indiziert, oder sollte ihr Einsatz strikt auf Notfallzulassungskontexte angesichts akuter Bedrohungen von pandemischem Ausmaß, äquivalent zum Auftreten von COVID-19, beschränkt bleiben? 2. In der täglichen klinischen Praxis dient das Management von grenzwertigem systolischem Blutdruck (z. B. 140/90 mmHg) und das LDL-Screening dazu, die empfindliche Innenauskleidung der Blutgefäße (das Endothel) vor kumulativen, stummen Mikroschäden zu schützen. Dieses proaktive Rahmenwerk greift, bevor sichtbare Symptome auftreten, mit dem alleinigen Ziel, den menschlichen Gefäßbaum zu bewahren. Bei der Evaluierung der systemischen Bioverteilung und der Multi-Passage-Perfusion von mRNA-LNP-Formulierungen bietet diese etablierte präventive Logik eine wertvolle Perspektive für translationale Sicherheitsmodelle. Die Erhaltung der endothelialen Gesundheit repräsentiert jedoch nur eine spezifische Facette innerhalb eines breiteren, multidimensionalen Bouquets von Forschungsparametern, die kollaborativ evaluiert werden können. Um eine umfassende Plattformcharakterisierung in der Post-Autorisierungsphase zu erreichen, schlägt diese gemeinsame Agenda eine gemeinsame Untersuchung der folgenden miteinander verknüpften Säulen vor: Die pharmakokinetische Säule: Korrelation präklinischer lokaler Deponierungsmodelle [2] mit Humandaten bezüglich der systemischen LNP-Zirkulation, der Multi-Passage-Gefäßexposition und der Clearance in tiefen Gewenben. Die biochemische und kinetische Säule: Überwachung der intrazellulären Langlebigkeit modifizierter, pseudouridinierter synthetischer mRNA-Stränge und der potenziellen longitudinalen Gewebepersistenz translatierter Antigene über ultrasensitive Diagnostik, einschließlich Single-Molecule-Array (Simoa)-Assays, massenspektrometrischer Quantifizierungen [4] und Protokollen zur extremen biologischen Haltbarkeit. title: Which Symptom Leads Depends on the Person
abstract_text: Early identification of psychological deterioration is often framed around finding a symptom sequence that generalizes across people: if some symptoms reliably precede others, a monitoring system could flag those earlier-moving symptoms before overall state has clearly worsened. We test this framing using a public intensive longitudinal EMA dataset of 40 individuals with generalized anxiety disorder or major depressive disorder, and find it does not hold. A group-averaged lead-lag ranking across 21 symptoms suggests positive affect, worry, and tension precede others, while depressed mood lags; computed separately per individual, direction is statistically indistinguishable from chance for every symptom (binomial tests, all p > .25). A noise-calibrated null model, using a moving block bootstrap to preserve temporal dependence, shows this disagreement exceeds what estimation error alone predicts for tension and depressed mood (p = .0014 and p < .001, Holm-adjusted p = .0042 and p = .0012), a pattern stable across a range of block lengths, though not for positive affect or worry (p = .254 and p = .051), consistent with genuine heterogeneity in two of four symptoms rather than insufficient power at N = 40. Mood inertia, by contrast, is consistent within individuals (82.5% individually significant), showing this washout is specific to sequence, not a general failure to detect structure. We report a secondary forecasting test that is directionally suggestive but not confirmed. These findings challenge a common assumption in psychopathology research: that population-level symptom dynamics generalize to individuals. Not every apparently coherent aggregate symptom direction reflects genuine heterogeneity, but some do, and these cannot be explained by estimation noise alone.

title: Chronic Smartphone Exposure as a Behavioral Science Problem: Toward a Life-Course Agenda for Health Research
abstract_text: Abstract Smartphones are now woven into everyday behavior across development, yet much of the evidence linking digital technology to health relies on broad exposure categories, sparse measurement, and age-siloed literatures. As a result, current research is poorly positioned to evaluate chronic smartphone exposure as a device-specific, developmentally situated phenomenon. This commentary does not argue that smartphones are inherently harmful or beneficial, nor does it claim that smartphone use causes long-term cognitive decline. Instead, it argues that existing research designs are insufficient for anticipating the developmental and lifespan health implications of chronic smartphone exposure. Evidence from youth links problematic or early smartphone use with mental health symptoms, sleep disruption, physical inactivity, obesity-related outcomes, and social relationship patterns, whereas studies of older adults often suggest that digital technology use may support cognitive aging through stimulation, compensation, and social connection. These literatures are not contradictory so much as incomplete, reflecting different cohorts, devices, contexts, and developmental periods. A life-course research agenda is needed that centers smartphone-specific measurement, intensive longitudinal methods, measurement-burst designs, passive sensing, digital phenotyping, and privacy-preserving governance for long-term behavioral data collection. Such an agenda would allow researchers to examine when, for whom, and under what conditions smartphone engagement intersects with modifiable behavioral and psychosocial risk domains relevant to cognitive health.

title: Metaheuristic-Optimized Deep Learning for Smart Solar Energy Management: A Comprehensive Review
abstract_text: The accurate forecasting of solar power generation is a cornerstone of smart energy management, directly affecting dispatch scheduling, battery storage operation, demand response, and the overall stability of grids with high photovoltaic (PV) penetration. Deep learning (DL) architectures, including long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, gated recurrent units (GRU), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and, more recently, attention-based transformers, have become the dominant tool for this task because of their capacity to model the nonlinear and non-stationary behaviour of solar irradiance and PV output. However, the predictive accuracy of these architectures is highly sensitive to their hyperparameters, and manual or grid-search tuning is computationally expensive and rarely converges to a global optimum. Metaheuristic optimization algorithms, inspired by evolutionary, swarm, physics-based, and human-based phenomena, have therefore been widely hybridized with DL models to automate and improve hyperparameter search, feature selection, and, in some cases, network weight optimization. This paper presents a structured and up-to-date review of metaheuristic-optimized deep learning algorithms for solar power and irradiance forecasting within smart energy management systems. We propose a taxonomy of the most commonly used metaheuristics, summarize the architectural characteristics of the deep learning backbones they are paired with, and synthesize quantitative results reported across recent studies, including Fire Hawk Optimization (FHO), the Improved Mountain Gazelle Optimizer (IMGO), the Evolutionary Mating Algorithm (EMA), the Reptile Search Algorithm (RSA), the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and the Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA). Comparative tables and figures illustrate the relative strengths, computational trade-offs, and reported accuracy gains of these hybrid frameworks, with several studies reporting coefficients of determination (R²) above 0.98 after metaheuristic tuning. The review concludes by identifying open challenges, including computational overhead, limited generalization across climates and PV technologies, and the scarcity of standardized benchmarks, and it outlines promising research directions such as multi-objective and explainable metaheuristic optimization for real-time smart-grid deployment.

title: Cascading cognitive failures in geometric proof construction: A qualitative study of prospective mathematics teachers
abstract_text: Constructing a valid geometric proof requires prospective mathematics teachers to coordinate premises, deductive warrants, proof goals, and representations. Although empirical studies have documented multiple proof-related difficulties, less is known about how a breakdown at one point constrains subsequent reasoning. This qualitative descriptive-exploratory study examined four direct proof tasks and task-based semi-structured interviews with six prospective mathematics teachers from an initial sample of 20. Data were analyzed using an adapted Explorative Mathematical Argumentation (EMA) framework composed of initiation, tools, goals, and modalities. A response was classified as a failure when both written and interview data indicated that the participant possessed relevant knowledge but did not use or apply it appropriately. Failures were present in all components of the EMA framework, and were most prevalent in the application of theorems and in the use of deductive logic. Within-participant analysis indicated possible pathways, as the under-integration of a premise limited access to an appropriate warrant; the use of a theorem without support resulted in invalid intermediate assertions, and disrupted the continuity of the argument; and the use of a theorem along with a drawing resulted in a lack of checking the theorem against the conditions. These pathways were not rigid but indicated the interplay of different conceptual, strategic, representational, and communicative demands. The results of the study provide support for a stage-differentiated and functionally interrelated description of proof, and for the construction of pathways of failure as a process-oriented description of gaps across different classifications of failure.

title: Música como motor narrativo en Ema: un análisis semiótico y corporal del universo sonoro

title: The Chameleon Neuron: Emergent Retention, Transmutation, and Abstention in a Continual-Learning Organism
abstract_text: We present the Chameleon Neuron, a continual-learning organism whose unit is a low-rankstem neuron with epigenetic marks and a context meta-selector, organized as a dynamicpopulation that grows by neurogenesis, specializes into niches, and consolidates offline.Rather than treating forgetting, domain adaptation and out-of-distribution (OOD) detectionas separate problems, we show that three capabilities coexist on one substrate, withoutbinary masks and without replay: retention (not forgetting), transmutation (classifyingknown-but-corrupted inputs), and abstention (rejecting true OOD). title: Evaluation of Large Language Models for Natural Language to SQL Query Generation: A Comparative Study Using Exact Match and Execution Accuracy
abstract_text: Decisions are being made based on data, and the demands for easy-to-use interfaces that enable users to simply type in a question to a relational database without having to be a Structured Query Language (SQL) expert have increased. Although the development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has seen remarkable advancements in the past few years, and has led to the emergence of LLMs that have significantly improved the generation of SQL from natural language (Text-to-SQL)[1], there is a relative lack of systematic comparisons between the latest commercial LLMs that has been tested against a series of graded SQL complexity levels with both syntactic and execution-based metrics. This research aims to assess and contrast ChatGPT, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, and Microsoft Copilot for their accuracy and efficacy in creating SQL queries from natural language queries. In a quantitative experimental design, 100 natural language questions were given using a purpose-built benchmark, with six types of queries that included simple retrieval, filtering, joins, aggregation, GROUP BY and HAVING, and nested subqueries. The results of the models were assessed using the manually written and validated ground truth query, with the use of normalised Exact Match Accuracy (EMA) and Execution Accuracy (EXA). The best overall results (EMA 97%, EXA 97%) were obtained by ChatGPT. The Copilot scored EMA 56% and EXA 96%, DeepSeek EMA 55% and EXA 93% and Gemini the lowest with a score of EMA 36% and EXA 87%. The large margin between EMA and EXA for the models (+51 points, +40 points, +38 points) demonstrates the significant shortcomings of exact-match scoring when it comes to assessing real-world skills for producing valid but structurally different SQL. The study empirically demonstrates comparative behaviours of the current LLMs, and suggests the use of execution-aware evaluation in the studies and deployment of Text-to-SQL.

title: Improving the Comparability of Momentary Affect Assessments: The Role of Item-Specific Effects in Within-Person Affect Dynamics
abstract_text: A primary objective of intensive longitudinal studies is to investigate within- person dynamics. In this context, item heterogeneity plays a critical role, as within-person processes may vary across items within a scale. A common exam- ple is the assessment of momentary affect using adjective lists (e.g., sad, angry, anxious, stressed), where each item captures different facets of positive or neg- ative affect, providing unique and non-interchangeable information. However, standard practices often overlook item heterogeneity by aggregating item scores or assuming a single within-person factor in dynamic structural equation mod- els. This simplification does not permit a fine-grained analysis of within-person dynamics and compromises cross-study comparability when item pools differ across studies. In this article, we reanalyze five large-scale intensive longitudinal datasets assessing momentary affect to illustrate how item heterogeneity can be explicitly modeled. We introduce a flexible modeling approach that accommo- dates item-specific and person-specific dynamics while improving comparability across studies, based on residualized dynamic structural equation modeling with reference items. We compare this method to conventional modeling strategies and provide practical guidance for addressing item heterogeneity in the analysis of intensive longitudinal data.

title: Exploring the Temporal Dynamics of Interpersonal Variability and Personality Functioning at Within- and Between-Person Levels
abstract_text:
Introduction: Behavioral and affective instability in interpersonal interactions, a common struggle for individuals with personality dysfunction, poses a significant challenge for clinicians and serves as a major obstacle preventing them from making progress in their lives. This study examined the relationship between interpersonal variability and personality functioning using multilevel modeling, as well as the unique explanatory power of interpersonal variability beyond its mean-level. 
Methods: This study combines a longitudinal approach with experience sampling features, collecting monthly data from 342 adults over six months. Personality functioning was assessed with the Level of Personality Functioning Scale Self-Report (LPFS-SR), and interpersonal behaviors (submissive, quarrelsome), perception of other’s behavior, and affects (positive and negative) were assessed with self-report measures.
Results: Variability in quarrelsome behavior, perception of other's behavior, and negative affect were significantly associated with personality functioning at within-person and between-person levels. However, the relationships between variability in submissive behavior, positive affect, and personality functioning diverged at each level. Moreover, variability in submissive behavior and perception of other's behavior accounted for additional variance beyond mean-levels. 
Conclusion: Results suggest the importance of considering not only the degree but also the temporal variability of interpersonal behaviors and affects in constructing personalized models of personality dysfunction.

title: Environmental risk assessment of antineoplastic drugs: A case study in Florianópolis, Southern Brazil
abstract_text: Antineoplastic drugs are extensively used in cancer therapy and are mainly released into the environment via patient excretion. Due to their toxicological, mutagenic, and cytostatic effects, these compounds may pose risks to aquatic ecosystems and human health. This study assessed antineoplastic drug consumption in the Florianópolis region (southern Brazil) over a 1-year period using data from two high-complexity oncology centers. A total of 43 drugs were identified, with capecitabine, hydroxycarbamide, and fluorouracil showing the highest consumption rates (140.2, 113.0, and 11.6 µg.inhab -1 .day -1 , respectively). An environmental risk assessment was conducted in accordance with the European Medicines Agency (EMA) framework. Predicted Environmental Concentrations (PECs) were estimated for all compounds, and 20 drugs met the criteria for Phase II evaluation, although only 13 could be evaluated due to the availability of ecotoxicological data. Risk Quotient (RQ) analysis indicated that only imatinib initially presented RQ > 1; however, its RQ decreased to 1 in Phase II tier B. Overall, no significant environmental risk was identified, with RQ values ranging from 0.325 (imatinib) to 1.1 × 10 − 6 (ifosfamide), well below moderate-risk thresholds. Physicochemical properties indicated bioconcentration potential for mitotane, tamoxifen, and diethylstilbestrol, and high persistence for vinblastine. These results reinforce the need for long-term, compound-specific monitoring and future regulatory guidelines for antineoplastic drugs as emerging contaminants.

title: A systematic review of abatacept and belatacept in immune-mediated diseases
abstract_text: BACKGROUND: Abatacept (ABA) and belatacept (BEL) are immunomodulatory fusion proteins in which the extracellular domain of cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) is linked to the Fc fragment of human IgG1. Functionally, they bind to cell surface antigens CD80 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells, thereby preventing CD28-mediated costimulatory signaling. This systematic review aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of ABA and BEL in immune-mediated diseases, focusing on indications currently not approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or the European Medicines Agency (EMA). METHODS: We searched PubMed and Web of Science for reports describing clinical efficacy of ABA or BEL in at least one patient with immune-mediated conditions outside FDA/EMA-approved indications. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses checklist guided our data reporting. RESULTS: Of 5333 articles initially extracted, 2778 unique records were screened after de-duplication, and 96 matched our criteria and were included in this study. ABA was beneficial in patients diagnosed with Sjögren's syndrome (particularly secondary forms); autoimmunity in association with immunodeficiency; early, inflammatory and normal-like subtypes of systemic sclerosis; scleroderma; arthritis in systemic lupus erythematosus; inflammatory myopathies (polymyositis, immune-mediated necrotizing myositis, and antisynthetase syndrome); and giant-cell arteritis. Lower-level evidence studies reported positive results using ABA to treat granulomatosis with polyangiitis; relapsing polychondritis; sarcoidosis; and inflammatory eye diseases. Results of several studies highlighted the positive impact of ABA on arthritis in patients taking this drug for other indications. Likewise, several autoimmune diseases responded effectively to ABA when used to treat concomitant rheumatoid arthritis. Positive serological responses suggesting downstream modulation of B cell activation were reported in several randomized controlled trials. BEL was used after kidney transplantation in patients with proteinuric kidney disease or lupus nephritis, and in a few non-transplanted CTLA-4 haploinsufficiency carriers for immunodeficiency-associated autoimmunity. CONCLUSIONS: Our results provide a comprehensive summary of the efficacy of ABA and BEL across a broad spectrum of autoimmune diseases.

title: Organic solvent-free micellar liquid chromatographic determination of amoxicillin, chlorzoxazone, and ibuprofen in pharmaceutical and biological matrices
abstract_text: Athletes are frequently prescribed combination therapies to manage bacterial infections and musculoskeletal injuries, often involving amoxicillin (AMX), ibuprofen (IBU), and chlorzoxazone (CHL). However, their co-administration presents analytical challenges due to the structural diversity of these drugs within complex matrices. Simultaneous quantification of these agents is particularly demanding in the context of pharmacokinetic studies, therapeutic drug monitoring, and pharmaceutical quality control, where sensitivity, selectivity, and matrix compatibility are essential. To address this challenge, the present study introduces a rapid, robust micellar liquid chromatographic (MLC) method demonstrating an environmentally favorable profile relative to conventional acetonitrile-based RP-HPLC comparators, for the simultaneous determination of AMX, CHL, and IBU in their combined pharmaceutical dosage forms, and human plasma samples. The method utilizes a short RP-C18 column i.e., 75 mm, with UV detection at 220 nm, achieving complete separation of all three analytes in under 6 min using a low impact micellar mobile phase composed of sodium lauryl sulfate (SDS), Brij-35, and potassium dihydrogen phosphate at pH 3.0. Method validation was performed according to ICH guidelines, demonstrating linearity (R² > 0.999), accuracy (98.6-101.1%), adequate sensitivity (LOD: 0.44-0.74 µg/mL; LOQ: 1.32-2.25 µg/mL), and excellent baseline resolution between adjacent peaks (Rs > 4.5) across the concentration range of 2.5-25 µg/mL for all three analytes. Environmental sustainability was quantitatively assessed; the proposed method achieved an Eco-scale score of 87, compared to 68-78 for previously reported RP-HPLC methods, providing a quantitative basis for the green chemistry comparison. In alignment with green chemistry principles, the method's environmental sustainability was further evaluated using multiple metrics including the Analytical Eco-Scale, GAPI, AGREE, BAGI, and RGB12 tools. The collective results indicate that the proposed method's environmental profile compares favorably with previously reported RP-HPLC procedures, though it is acknowledged that the applied greenness metrics do not fully capture potential environmental persistence of non-ionic surfactants such as Brij-35 at high concentrations. Within the validated scope, the method demonstrates preliminary suitability for pharmaceutical quality control and therapeutic concentration monitoring; full bioanalytical validation per FDA/EMA guidance is recommended prior to pharmacokinetic applications. It is acknowledged that acetonitrile use in the plasma preparation step is included in the environmental assessments, and that long-term sustainability of the surfactant system at high concentrations warrants further evaluation.

title: Ecological momentary assessment in adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus: A scoping review
abstract_text: AIMS: To conduct a scoping review of the application of ecological momentary assessment (EMA) in adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1DM), providing references for future research and practice in this field. METHODS: This review followed the JBI scoping review methodology framework and systematically searched 10 databases, including CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, CBM, PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, EMbase, PsycINFO and CINAHL, from the establishment of the databases to 29 September 2025. The included literature was summarised and analysed. RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included. EMA was used to investigate self-management, glycaemic control, psychosocial factors and cognitive function in adolescents with T1DM. Key findings revealed dynamic, real-time associations: self-management behaviours showed time- and context-dependent effects on glycaemic control (e.g. higher risk of omissions in mornings or social situations); affect and glucose levels exhibited bidirectional interactions, with negative affect impairing and positive affect improving glycaemic stability; social environment (peer and family support) and cognitive function (e.g. executive function) significantly moderated management outcomes. Most identified associations were within-person and contemporaneous; few studies examined between-person differences or time-lagged predictive effects. EMA demonstrated acceptable feasibility across diverse protocols. However, considerable methodological heterogeneity existed across studies, and most evidence was limited to Western populations. CONCLUSION: EMA is a feasible method for managing type 1 diabetes in adolescents and is capable of capturing real-time, dynamic associations among behaviour, affect, social context and glycaemic control. Future research should prioritise methodological standardisation, develop culturally adapted assessment tools and explore real-time intervention strategies to enable precise and personalised diabetes management. From a clinical perspective, EMA can guide individualised care by identifying high-risk time windows (e.g. mornings), social contexts (e.g. peer dining) and emotional triggers (e.g. negative affect), supporting targeted patient education, just-in-time behavioural reminders and collaborative mental health interventions.

title: FADED: unlocking few-shot defect detection via frequency-domain augmentation and distillation enhancement
abstract_text: Few-Shot Object Detection (FSOD) is particularly relevant to industrial defect inspection, where defects are rare, heterogeneous, and labeled data are scarce. FADED combines Frequency-Domain Data Augmentation (FDDA) to synthesize diverse defect appearances by Fourier-domain fusion (leveraging the common phase/structure vs. amplitude/style intuition), and Multi-source Online Distillation and Alignment (MODA) to stabilize fine-tuning with an EMA teacher and multi-level alignment (feature/RPN/logit) plus logit standardization. title: Anti-Fireblight Potential of the Non-Ribosomal Templated Fabclavines, Synthesized by <em>Xenorhabdus szentirmaii </em>(EMC) and <em>X. budapestensis</em> (EMA)
abstract_text: The options for controlling agricultural plant-pathogenic bacterial diseases with antibiotics are rather limited. Applications of naturally derived antimicrobial peptides may provide an alternative. Background/Objectives: The cell-free conditioned media (CFCM) of Xenorhabdus budapestensis (EMA) and X. szentirmaii (EMC) bacteria inactivate Erwinia amylovora, the causative agent of fire blight disease in Rosaceae both in vitro and in planta. We suppose that the active ingredient compounds are fabclavines. Testing the hypothesis, inducible fabclavine-producing strains were constructed in regulatory gene (hfq) deleted mutant strains of both Xenorhabdus species. Anti-Erwinia potentials of non-induced and induced fabclavine-producing cultures were compared in vitro and in planta. Methods: To obtain the appropriate fabclavine-producing mutants, we applied the easyPACId method with minor modifications. Fabclavine production was confirmed by LC-HRMS and in vitro bioassays. The in planta experiments were designed and carried out as follows: apple blossoms in an incubator were subjected to antimicrobial and control treatments before artificial inoculations of the buds with Erwinia amylovora Ea1. Results: Cell-free medium of both induced fabclavine-producing Xenorhabdus species exerted strong antagonistic effects on Ea1 in vitro, while the non-induced ones showed substantially reduced antibacterial activity. Similarly, both induced culture media prevented fireblight symptoms in artificially infected flowers in a dose-dependent manner. The non-induced EMC was completely inactive in planta, whereas EMA exhibited some protective activity. Conclusions: The results support the hypothesis that inducible Xenorhabdus mutants producing only fabclavines can be used for protection against E. amylovora. Application perspectives are discussed from the aspects of resistance, side effects, and costs based on parallel in planta experiments with streptomycin and kasugamycin.

title: Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions to Reduce Sedentary Behavior and Promote Physical Activity in Patients With Chronic Disease: Scoping Review
abstract_text: Background: Patients with chronic diseases often struggle to maintain sufficient physical activity (PA) and reduce sedentary behavior in daily life. Just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs), delivered through mobile health technologies such as mobile apps, wearable devices, sensors, and ecological momentary assessment, offer timely and personalized support based on individuals' changing needs. However, the evidence base for their use in promoting PA and reducing sedentary behavior among patients with chronic diseases remains fragmented. Objective: This review aimed to describe study characteristics and design features of JITAIs, summarize reported evaluation findings related to PA and sedentary behavior, and identify barriers and facilitators related to engagement and use of JITAIs. Methods: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Scopus from database inception to June 2025. Two researchers independently screened the records, selected eligible studies, and performed data charting to ensure rigor and consistency. Results: A total of 14 studies were included in this review. Of these, 6 primarily targeted PA, 1 focused solely on sedentary behavior, and 5 addressed both PA and sedentary behavior. Of the remaining, 6 studies provided preliminary evidence supporting the positive effects of JITAIs in promoting PA among individuals with chronic diseases, while 3 studies suggested positive effects on reducing sedentary behavior. Barriers and facilitators influencing the use of JITAIs in this population were identified. Barriers included technological usability and literacy, burden and intrusiveness of the intervention, perceived value and acceptability, external and contextual barriers, and privacy and data security concerns. Facilitators included enhanced motivation and behavioral engagement, increased awareness and self-monitoring, usability and integration into daily life, timely and personalized support, and support from health care professionals and the care environment. Conclusions: This scoping review identified preliminary evidence suggesting that JITAIs may help reduce sedentary behavior and promote PA among patients with chronic diseases. However, more large-scale, high-quality randomized controlled trial studies are needed to strengthen evidence and generalizability.

title: Sighing Dynamics as a Candidate Digital Biomarker for Anxiety in Daily Life Using Wearable Respiratory Monitoring: Intensive Longitudinal Study
abstract_text: Background: Sighing has been proposed as a primary respiratory reset mechanism that is often linked to emotional regulation. However, evidence linking sighing to anxiety relies heavily on laboratory studies, which lack ecological validity. It remains unclear whether ambulatory sighing dynamics in free-living settings reflect momentary (state) symptom fluctuations or enduring (trait) pathology.
