title: Ecological momentary assessment to uncover affect dynamics in patients with hereditary angioedema: a complementary tool for enhancing quality of life evaluation
abstract_text: <title>Abstract</title> Hereditary Angioedema (HAE) is a rare genetic condition associated with poor quality of life (QoL). Affect, defined by Activation (energy) and Valence (pleasantness), is linked to QoL and fluctuates daily, reflecting emotion regulation processes. This study explored affective dynamics in HAE patients, with (HAE A <sup>+</sup> ) and without attacks (HAE A <sup>−</sup> ), comparing them to healthy controls (CTR), using Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA). Secondarily, correlation between affective dynamics and AE-QoL was assessed. In this observational study, 12 HAE patients and 14 CTR completed weekly EMA surveys over 16 weeks, assessing Positive Activation (PA), Negative Activation (NA), and Valence (VA). Affective intensity, variability, and instability were computed. HAE participants also completed the AE-QoL and AECT. HAE patients showed higher mean VA (p = 0.016) and lower NA for worry (p = 0.021) than CTR. HAE A <sup>−</sup> had higher PA and VA, and lower NA for anger and worry than both HAE A <sup>+</sup> and CTR. AE-QoL correlated negatively with PA (r=–0.78, p = 0.003) and VA (r=–0.68, p = 0.014). HAE patients, especially those without attacks, displayed more positive emotional profiles than controls. EMA captured emotional patterns not evident in traditional questionnaires, supporting its value as a complementary tool for QoL evaluation in rare chronic diseases.

title: Improving the Performance of Recycled Multilayer PET Through Reactive Compatibilization Strategies
abstract_text: The recycling of post-industrial multilayer polyethylene terephthalate (mPET) packaging waste remains a major challenge due to the coexistence of incompatible polymeric phases and the deterioration of properties during reprocessing. In this work, different reactive compatibilization strategies were evaluated to improve the processability and performance of recycled multilayer PET scraps generated during industrial packaging manufacturing processes. Several functional compatibilizers were investigated, including poly(ethylene-co-acrylic acid) (EAA), poly(ethylene-alt-maleic anhydride) (EMA), poly(ethylene-co-glycidyl methacrylate) (EGMA), poly(ethylene-co-methyl acrylate-co-glycidyl methacrylate) (EMAGMA), and maleic anhydride (MA). The influence of compatibilization on the thermal, mechanical, chemical, surface, and morphological properties of recycled mPET was systematically analyzed. Processing behavior revealed that EMA- and MA-based formulations could not be successfully injection molded. In contrast, EAA-, EGMA-, and EMAGMA-based formulations showed suitable processability and enabled the production of defect-free specimens. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed only minor changes in thermal degradation behavior after compatibilization. In contrast, differential scanning calorimetry revealed changes in the melting behavior of the recycled formulations, while tensile and impact tests demonstrated marked improvements in ductility and toughness for EGMA- and EMAGMA-modified systems. Among them, EMAGMA provided the highest elongation at break and impact resistance. Contact angle measurements showed moderate changes in surface wettability, whereas density and hardness remained largely unaffected. FESEM analysis revealed a more homogeneous phase distribution and reduced dispersed-domain size in the compatibilized formulations, particularly for EGMA, indicating improved interfacial compatibility. These results demonstrate that glycidyl methacrylate-based compatibilizers are effective reactive agents for upgrading post-industrial multilayer PET waste into higher-performance recycled materials for different applications.

title: Substance Use and Risk for Suicide: Experiences of High-Risk Postpartum Women, Oregon and Utah, 2023-2024
abstract_text: Suicide is one of the leading causes of preventable death for postpartum women, and substance use is a known risk factor for suicide in this population. Despite this, trajectories of substance use across the perinatal period and associations with suicidal thoughts and behaviors have not been examined. In line with CPO’s aim of improving the well-being of individuals, families, and communities affected by the opioid crisis, the overall objective of the current proposal is to develop a preliminary knowledge base on the association between suicidality and substance use across the perinatal period. We will accomplish this by building off an existing longitudinal study of suicidality in high-risk pregnant and postpartum women (2/3 of whom are currently experiencing suicidal thoughts and behaviors, and/or have in the past). Our long-term goal is to utilize information gleaned toward proposing an R01 that would examine substance use in high-risk new mothers at a larger scale. Aim 1 is to examine concurrent associations between substance use and suicidal thoughts and behaviors at three timepoints: 6 weeks, 4 months, and 8 months postpartum. Aim 2 is to examine trajectories of substance use abstinence and relapse across the three timepoints. Aim 3 is to examine mechanisms of substance use relapse in postpartum women using daily diary data to assess the intercorrelations between parenting stress, emotion regulation, and substance use at each timepoint.

UniJEPA: A Unified Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Task-Agnostic Visual World Modeling
abstract_text: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) have emerged as a principled framework for self-supervised learning of world models in compact latent spaces, yet existing methods are fragmented: some predict masked parts of a single image in latent space (I-JEPA), others learn to predict global photometric transformations (Image World Models), while video-scale JEPAs predict future temporal states and are post-trained for action-conditioned planning (V-JEPA~2, DINO-World, DINO-WM). These objectives are treated as distinct recipes with separate encoders, predictors, and anti-collapse regularizers, hindering a single model from unifying image-level and video-level world modeling. We present UniJEPA, a unified JEPA that jointly learns photometric prediction (image-level transformations) and temporal prediction (video-level next-state dynamics) in one shared latent space. A single end-to-end objective, composed of a next-embedding prediction loss and a Gaussian regularizer, yields a provably anti-collapse encoder-predictor pair trainable from raw pixels without EMA, stop-gradient, or pre-trained encoders. We show that the same latent space supports controllable abstraction: photometric prediction learns invariant structure while temporal prediction learns equivariant dynamics. After action-conditioned post-training on offline trajectories, UniJEPA enables zero-shot planning by treating goal features as prediction targets. On image, video, and control benchmarks, UniJEPA matches or surpasses task-specific JEPAs while requiring a single loss hyperparameter, and plans up to tens of times faster than generative world models at comparable accuracy.

title: Where Is the Mind? From the Individual-Interior Model to Generative-Resonance Psychology ーA Relational Ontology of Optimism, Resilience, Mindfulness, Emotion, and Consciousness
abstract_text: Short Description This paper proposes Generative-Resonance Psychology, a relational ontology that challenges the conventional assumption that the mind consists primarily of psychological states, traits, capacities, and representations located inside the individual. It argues that psychological phenomena emerge through the ongoing interaction of embodied generative potential and relational resonance, expressed as E = ΦR. Within this framework, optimism, resilience, mindfulness, emotion, selfhood, and consciousness are temporary and self-sensing crystallizations of participation rather than independently possessed inner attributes. Psychological suffering is reconstructed as the obstruction or repetitive closure of generative participation, while clinical practice and social policy are reoriented toward restoring pathways for renewed participation rather than merely strengthening isolated individuals. Book Description Modern psychology has achieved remarkable scientific and clinical success by treating the individual as its primary unit of analysis. Emotions, beliefs, personality traits, psychological capacities, diagnoses, and consciousness are commonly described as states or functions located within the individual and influenced by an external social and material environment. This paper asks whether that methodological division has gradually become an ontological assumption. Where Is the Mind? develops an alternative framework called Generative-Resonance Psychology. Rather than understanding existence through the implicit equation E = S, in which a person becomes identified with a currently crystallized psychological state, the paper proposes E = ΦR: existence emerges through the conjunction of situated generative potential, Φ, and relational resonance, R. Psychological life is modeled as the recursive cycle: Φ → R → S → Φ′ Generative possibility enters relation, takes temporary form as a psychological state S, and returns to the relational field as renewed possibility Φ′. Emotion, identity, psychological capacity, and conscious experience are therefore real but provisional crystallizations within an ongoing generative process. When this circulation remains open, psychological states can change, relationships can be renegotiated, and new forms of participation can emerge. When the cycle becomes closed, however, psychological states may reproduce themselves through: S → S′ → S″ This pattern, termed Hyper-S, provides a common theoretical structure for rumination, compulsive repetition, fixed pessimism, self-negation, diagnostic identity fixation, excessive self-monitoring, and institutional forms of permanent evaluation. The framework produces several major reinterpretations of established psychological concepts. Mindfulness is reconstructed as participation in present ΦR rather than simply an individually possessed attentional skill. Optimism becomes participation in future ΦR: the lived sense that the present does not completely determine what may emerge. Resilience becomes renewed participation after disruption rather than restoration of an earlier state. Its generative form is not S1 → S1, but S1 → ΦR → S2. Individual psychological capacities are not denied. Instead, they are interpreted as embodied memories of previous participation. Experiences of being supported after failure, receiving response when vulnerable, recovering from disruption, or successfully re-entering relationships leave bodily, affective, cognitive, and narrative traces. What appears as an individual psychological strength may therefore be understood as past relationships retained as present generative possibility. This argument leads to a three-layer model of psychological capacity: Ct = f(Pt, Mt, MPt) where Ct is the capacity expressed at time t, Pt is present ΦR participation, Mt is accumulated participatory memory, and MPt is meta-participation. Pleasure and displeasure are similarly repositioned. They are interpreted as local self-sensings of changes in ΦR rather than ultimate causes of desire. Immediate pleasure is not identical to long-term generative expansion. Short-term pleasure may coexist with d(ΦR)/dt < 0, while temporary discomfort may coexist with d(ΦR)/dt > 0. Emotion is consequently understood as an embodied mode of person–world participation. Fear senses rapidly closing future possibility; anger senses obstructed relation while agency remains; grief reorganizes existence after the loss of an important relation; joy accompanies newly opened possibility; relief registers restoration of a threatened generative cycle; shame converts relational exclusion into apparent negation of the whole self; and guilt senses harm to another person’s or a shared relation’s ΦR. The framework further extends to consciousness. Rather than treating consciousness solely as the unexplained transition from physical brain state Sphysical to phenomenal state Sphenomenal, the paper asks whether part of the hard problem arises from first dividing a single embodied process into objective and subjective crystallizations. Consciousness is provisionally reconceived as self-sensing ΦR participation: the process through which changes in person–world relation are lived as changes in one’s own existence and recursively influence what happens next. The paper explicitly presents this as a reframing rather than a complete solution to the phenomenal hard problem. Clinical implications follow directly. Psychological suffering is understood not merely as dysfunction inside the individual but as the obstruction, contraction, interruption, or repetitive closure of generative participation. Clinical practice therefore expands from repairing individual dysfunction toward investigating bodily, interpersonal, material, organizational, and institutional conditions that maintain closure. The clinician becomes not merely a repair technician but a responsible participant in reopening generative pathways. At the societal level, this produces a shift from the ideal of the strong individual toward the design of a restartable society: a society in which failure does not eliminate belonging, temporary incapacity does not eliminate material security, harmful relationships can be exited, alternative roles remain available, and people are not forced to display immediate recovery as evidence of worth. Finally, the paper outlines an empirical research program based on the analytical unit: Person × Relation × Environment × Time Φ, R, S, and Hyper-S are operationalized through multidimensional indicators rather than collapsed into a single score. Longitudinal studies, experience sampling, interaction observation, relational network analysis, clinical process research, natural experiments, intervention comparisons, and multilevel biological–psychological–social data are proposed to test the framework. The criterion d(ΦR)/dt ≥ 0 is therefore not proposed as a numerical utility function or optimization target. It functions as a directional diagnostic question: whether the relevant person–world system is preserving, reopening, or progressively closing the possibilities of meaningful participation over time. The paper ultimately proposes a change in psychology’s foundational object of inquiry: from the mind as something the individual possesses to the movement through which mind emerges. Highlights Proposes Generative-Resonance Psychology as a relational ontology of psychological life. Replaces the implicit ontology E = S with E = ΦR, where Φ represents situated generative potential and R represents relational resonance. Models psychological generation through the recursive cycle Φ → R → S → Φ′. Defines Hyper-S as the self-reproducing closure S → S′ → S″, linking rumination, compulsion, identity fixation, self-surveillance, and institutional evaluation. Reinterprets optimism, resilience, and mindfulness as future, regenerative, and present forms of ΦR participation, rather than isolated psychological traits. Explains relatively stable psychological capacities as embodied memories of previous generative participation. Introduces the three-layer capacity model Ct = f(Pt, Mt, MPt), integrating present participation, participatory memory, and meta-participation. Distinguishes affective valence from generative direction, showing why immediate pleasure need not indicate long-term flourishing. Reconceptualizes emotion as an embodied and self-sensing mode of person–world participation. Reframes consciousness as self-sensing ΦR participation while explicitly retaining the unresolved phenomenal hard problem. Reconstructs psychological suffering as the closure or repetitive fixation of generative participation rather than exclusively as individual dysfunction. Expands clinical intervention across intrapersonal, interpersonal, material, organizational, and institutional levels. Replaces the social ideal of the strong individual with that of a restartable society. Proposes Person × Relation × Environment × Time as the primary unit for empirical investigation. Treats d(ΦR)/dt ≥ 0 as a directional diagnostic criterion rather than a numerical optimization target. Part-by-Part Summary Part I. The Formation of the Individual-Interior Model Part I traces how modern psychology came to locate the mind within the bounded individual. The methodological isolation of cognition, emotion, personality, and behavior gradually became an ontology in which psychological states were treated as internally possessed entities. Classification and measurement transformed dynamic experience into traits, diagnoses, and capacities S. Positive psychology shifted attention from deficit to strength but often retained the same individual-interior ontology, replacing negative S with positive S rather than questioning E = S itself. title: Revisiting the Benefit–Risk Profile of COVID‑19 Vaccines of the Italian Vaccination Campaign
abstract_text: Abstract Vaccination against COVID-19 represented one of the main public health strategies to reduce mortality, hospitalizations, and complications. In this context, pharmacovigilance played an essential role in the continuous monitoring of the benefit-risk profile of authorized vaccines, enabling the timely identification of rare adverse events and the implementation of risk minimization measures. This work revisits the post-marketing surveillance system for COVID-19 vaccines in Italy, with particular attention to signal detection mechanisms, risk management, and the main safety signals that emerged during the first year of the vaccination campaign. Data from the National Pharmacovigilance Network, periodic safety reports, EMA/PRAC documents, and AIFA communications were considered. The analysis highlights how, following the widespread use of mRNA and adenoviral vector vaccines, adverse events of special interest emerged, including vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia, myocarditis/pericarditis, and other rare events, which led to updates of the Summary of Product Characteristics, the Package Leaflet, and communications to healthcare professionals. The data confirm that the benefit-risk ratio of COVID-19 vaccines remained favorable. The study emphasizes the effectiveness of the regulatory and pharmacovigilance architecture implemented in Italy and Europe in supporting rapid, evidence-based decisions in the context of a pandemic emergency. Keywords: COVID-19; Vaccines; Adverse reactions

title: Methodological Perspectives and Pharmacodynamic Considerations in mRNA-LNP Platform Evaluation: A Socratic Compendium of Unresolved Pathophysiological Open Questions by the Vascular Pharmacodynamic and Autoimmunity Research Core Group (VPARCG)
abstract_text: Methodological Perspectives and Pharmacodynamic Considerations in mRNA-LNP Platform Evaluation: A Socratic Compendium of Unresolved Pathophysiological Open Questions by the Vascular Pharmacodynamic and Autoimmunity Research Core Group (VPARCG) Author: Vascular Pharmacodynamic and Autoimmunity Research Core Group (VPARCG)Digital Object Identifier (DOI): 10.5281/zenodo.21840325Keywords: mRNA platform pharmacokinetics, Lipid Nanoparticles, Endotheliitis, Self-Controlled Case Series, ICH GCP compliance, Vascular safety, Simoa antigen persistence Abstract After almost six years of global deployment of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated messenger RNA (mRNA) platforms, even for medical professionals working for decades there are still open questions, e.g., whether significant gaps remain between structural molecular pharmacokinetics / pharmacodynamics data translations from animal to human models and proactive clinical surveillance methodologies while knowing that this immunisation technique is of a totally different kind compared to conventional vaccines. It was developed during emergency conditions, leaving parameters regarding drug-drug interactions, long-term carcinogenicity, and novel lipid tissue-toxicity structurally designated for post-marketing evaluation under the accelerated initial licensure framework. Evoking historical precedents, the thalidomide lesson mandates proactive toxicological validation, while the corticosteroid paradigm warns against unmonitored latent attrition. The official WHO framework notes that because mRNA-LNP constructs represent a new technological class, several mechanistic questions remain that warrant ongoing data monitoring and proactive safety evaluations. These questions, therefore, need to be answered. Besides these questions, this VPARCG paper outlines 80 interconnected, non-evaluated pathophysiological and methodological questions surrounding first and second-generation mRNA formulations (including COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus [RSV] and seasonal influenza constructs (INF)). By framing these as open scientific questions the VPARCG - drawing from three decades of clinical experience in immunology / rheumatology and clinical epidemiology - seeks to provide a systematic roadmap for regulatory agencies and manufacturers to achieve more scientific clarity through objective, human-derived data in the post-marketing phase. 1. Introduction: The Imperative of Epistemic Clarity The continuous advancement of modern medicine relies on a transparent, productive dialogue between preclinical models, clinical practice, and regulatory oversight. After six years of global experience with lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated mRNA platforms (including COVID-19, RSV, and Influenza formulations), regulatory agencies and legislators share a vital mission: to strengthen public trust by gathering advanced, human-derived post-marketing safety data [1]. This memorandum is explicitly not an indictment of regulatory past actions. Instead, it serves as a proposed constructive resource and scientific compass based on long-standing clinical expert opinion. It aims to build a collaborative bridge (e.g., for the United States: between the Food and Drug Administration (FDA/CBER) and the legislative committees of the US Congress (Senate and House of Representatives), the healthcare leadership at present under Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and leading regulatory experts like FDA/CBER Leadership, as well as for all other countries). The goal is to establish a shared research agenda that harmonizes innovative technology with the foundational principle of primum non nocere. Furthermore, this initiative is designed as an ongoing, living project to be continuously updated over the coming years via the Zenodo server of CERN under the permanent Concept DOI (see above). The cornerstone of evidence-based medicine relies on the continuous reconciliation of preclinical models with real-world clinical observations. Over the past six years, the rapid translation of the mRNA-LNP platform from an investigational modality to a foundational public health tool has altered the landscape of preventive medicine. However, despite extensive statistical data regarding macrovascular clinical endpoints, several core mechanistic and methodological questions remain unaddressed in the public consensus and regulatory documentation. Clinical professionals are bound by the principles of primum non nocere to continuously audit the biological plausibility of mass-applied therapeutics. To support this ongoing scientific dialogue, this memorandum formalizes a structured catalog of fundamental questions for systematic evaluation and resolution by regulatory bodies (such as the FDA and EMA) and the pharmaceutical industry in the coming years. Only through human-derived, objective kinetic data can true scientific clarity and robust public trust be achieved. Ultimately, this framework serves to answer the definitive question clinical professionals pose at present: Is a broad, mass-market utilization of this newly implemented, non-fully-characterized platform technology medically indicated, or should its deployment be strictly restricted to emergency authorization contexts in the face of acute, pandemic-scale threats equivalent to the COVID-19 emergence? 2. In evaluating the systemic biodistribution and multi-passage perfusion of mRNA-LNP formulations, this established preventative logic offers a valuable perspective for translational safety models. title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing into Automated Adverse Event Signal Detection: A Comprehensive Review of Frameworks, Real-World Data, and Regulatory Challenges
abstract_text: Pharmacovigilance, the science of detecting, assessing, and preventing adverse effects of medicines, has traditionally relied on spontaneous reporting systems and manually applied disproportionality statistics to generate safety signals. The explosive growth in the volume and diversity of drug-safety-relevant data -- spanning structured spontaneous report databases, electronic health records, clinical narratives, social media, and other real-world data sources -- has outpaced the practical capacity of manual and purely statistical signal-detection workflows. This review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and natural language processing (NLP) are being integrated into automated adverse event signal detection, synthesising the current landscape of computational frameworks, real-world data sources, and the regulatory challenges that accompany their adoption. We describe the evolution from classical disproportionality methods -- the Proportional Reporting Ratio, Reporting Odds Ratio, Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network, and Multi-item Gamma Poisson Shrinker -- toward machine-learning and deep-learning architectures capable of learning complex, non-linear associations across heterogeneous data. Particular attention is given to the role of transformer-based language models, including BioBERT, ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT, and SpanBERT, in extracting adverse drug event mentions from unstructured clinical notes, biomedical literature, and social media text, and to hybrid frameworks that combine structured disproportionality analysis with unstructured-text mining and graph-based relational modelling. The review further surveys the principal real-world data infrastructures underpinning modern pharmacovigilance -- the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System, the WHO global individual case safety report database VigiBase, EudraVigilance, the FDA Sentinel Initiative, and the EMA's DARWIN EU platform -- and considers how AI-based tools are being layered onto these systems for federated querying, duplicate detection, and case-processing automation. Finally, the review addresses the regulatory and governance challenges that currently constrain routine adoption of AI-augmented signal detection, including model transparency and explainability, validation and performance monitoring, algorithmic bias, data privacy, and the evolving guidance issued by the FDA, EMA, ICH, and CIOMS, concluding with a forward-looking assessment of the conditions under which AI/NLP-based signal detection is likely to become an accepted, auditable component of routine drug safety surveillance.

title: CRISE SANITÁRIA E INOVAÇÃO FARMACOLÓGICA: UMA ANÁLISE MULTIDIMENSIONAL DO USO DA TIRZEPATIDA (MOUNJARO) E OS DESAFIOS DA VIGILÂNCIA NO BRASIL
abstract_text: A obesidade e o diabetes mellitus tipo 2 constituem importantes desafios para a saúde pública mundial devido à elevada prevalência, ao caráter crônico e à associação com múltiplas complicações metabólicas e cardiovasculares. Nesse contexto, a tirzepatida (Mounjaro®), agonista dual dos receptores do peptídeo insulinotrópico dependente de glicose (GIP) e do peptídeo semelhante ao glucagon tipo 1 (GLP-1), destaca-se como uma inovação terapêutica no controle glicêmico e na redução do peso corporal. O estudo teve como objetivo analisar, sob uma perspectiva multidimensional, a eficácia terapêutica da tirzepatida no tratamento da obesidade e do diabetes mellitus tipo 2, bem como os riscos decorrentes do uso irracional, da automedicação, da circulação de produtos irregulares e dos desafios relacionados à farmacovigilância e à vigilância sanitária no Brasil. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, de abordagem qualitativa, fundamentada em artigos científicos indexados nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO e Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde, complementada por documentos técnicos e regulatórios da ANVISA, FDA e EMA, publicados entre 2019 e 2026. As evidências demonstram que a tirzepatida proporciona reduções expressivas da hemoglobina glicada e do peso corporal, conforme observado nos estudos dos programas SURPASS e SURMOUNT. Entretanto, seu uso inadequado, impulsionado por demandas estéticas e pelo comércio clandestino, aumenta os riscos de eventos adversos e compromete a segurança dos pacientes. Conclui-se que os benefícios clínicos da tirzepatida dependem de prescrição criteriosa, acompanhamento multiprofissional, fortalecimento das ações de farmacovigilância e fiscalização sanitária, associados à educação em saúde para promoção do uso racional do medicamento.

title: Exploring the Temporal Dynamics of Interpersonal Variability and Personality Functioning at Within- and Between-Person Levels
abstract_text: Introduction: Behavioral and affective instability in interpersonal interactions, a common struggle for individuals with personality dysfunction, poses a significant challenge for clinicians and serves as a major obstacle preventing them from making progress in their lives. This study examined the relationship between interpersonal variability and personality functioning using multilevel modeling, as well as the unique explanatory power of interpersonal variability beyond its mean-level. Methods: This study combines a longitudinal approach with experience sampling features, collecting monthly data from 342 adults over six months. Personality functioning was assessed with the Level of Personality Functioning Scale Self-Report (LPFS-SR), and interpersonal behaviors (submissive, quarrelsome), perception of other’s behavior, and affects (positive and negative) were assessed with self-report measures. Results: Variability in quarrelsome behavior, perception of other's behavior, and negative affect were significantly associated with personality functioning at within-person and between-person levels. However, the relationships between variability in submissive behavior, positive affect, and personality functioning diverged at each level. Moreover, variability in submissive behavior and perception of other's behavior accounted for additional variance beyond mean-levels. Conclusion: Results suggest the importance of considering not only the degree but also the temporal variability of interpersonal behaviors and affects in constructing personalized models of personality dysfunction.

title: UniJEPA: A Unified Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Task-Agnostic Visual World Modeling
abstract_text: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) have emerged as a principled framework for self-supervised learning of world models in compact latent spaces, yet existing methods are fragmented: some predict masked parts of a single image in latent space (I-JEPA), others learn to predict global photometric transformations (Image World Models), while video-scale JEPAs predict future temporal states and are post-trained for action-conditioned planning (V-JEPA~2, DINO-World, DINO-WM). These objectives are treated as distinct recipes with separate encoders, predictors, and anti-collapse regularizers, hindering a single model from unifying image-level and video-level world modeling. We present UniJEPA, a unified JEPA that jointly learns photometric prediction (image-level transformations) and temporal prediction (video-level next-state dynamics) in one shared latent space. A single end-to-end objective, composed of a next-embedding prediction loss and a Gaussian regularizer, yields a provably anti-collapse encoder-predictor pair trainable from raw pixels without EMA, stop-gradient, or pre-trained encoders. We show that the same latent space supports controllable abstraction: photometric prediction learns invariant structure while temporal prediction learns equivariant dynamics. After action-conditioned post-training on offline trajectories, UniJEPA enables zero-shot planning by treating goal features as prediction targets. On image, video, and control benchmarks, UniJEPA matches or surpasses task-specific JEPAs while requiring a single loss hyperparameter, and plans up to tens of times faster than generative world models at comparable accuracy.

title: Enhancing Performance and User Engagement in Everyday Stress Monitoring: A Context-Aware Active Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract_text: Accurate stress monitoring in everyday settings requires informative labels without excessive user burden. Ecological Momentary Assessments (EMAs) provide self-reported labels, but poorly timed or frequent prompts can reduce their utility. This paper presents a context-aware active reinforcement learning algorithm for stress detection using photoplethysmography (PPG) from smartwatches and contextual data from smartphones. The algorithm uses the user's current context and response history to decide when to trigger an EMA. We first evaluate context-aware label selection in an offline study and then deploy the approach for real-time EMA triggering in a separate online cohort. Under the reported evaluation, Random Forest F1 increased from 0.21 for the offline cohort to 0.32 for the online cohort; adding contextual features increased it to 0.36. Personalization increased AUC by up to 0.10 across Random Forest, XGBoost, and SVM classifiers. These results support context-aware EMA scheduling and personalized modeling for real-world stress monitoring, while differences between the study cohorts limit causal attribution of the observed performance gains.

title: Primary acinic cell carcinoma of the breast: insights from a nine-case series and comprehensive literature review
abstract_text: To better understand primary acinic cell carcinoma (AcCC) of the breast, this study investigated its clinical and pathological features. Nine cases of primary acinic cell carcinoma were thoroughly evaluated using routine pathological and immunohistochemical methods. The clinical features, pathological morphological features, and prognosis of each case were collected and analyzed. The tumors were located in the left breast in four cases (44.4%) and the right breast in five (55.6%). Most lesions (88.9%, 8/9) were in the upper outer quadrant, with one (11.1%) in the lower outer quadrant. One case (11.1%) was categorized as BI-RADS 6, and eight (88.9%) as BI-RADS 4. Histologically, the cases exhibited diverse growth patterns. The predominant patterns were microglandular and acinar. Less common patterns included microcystic, cystic, follicular, clear cell, and solid structures. Eosinophilic secretions were visible within the lumens.The tumor cells showed cytoplasmic variations (granular, clear, or basophilic) and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemically, all tumors were negative for estrogen receptor (ER) and androgen receptor (AR). Progesterone receptor (PR) was weakly positive in two cases and negative in the remaining seven. Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) immunohistochemistry was negative in five cases and scored 1 + in four. Alpha-1-antichymotrypsin (AACT) was positive in four cases, while lysozyme was positive in eight. Collagen IV was negative in all cases, whereas epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) was diffusely positive. S100 protein expression was detected in seven cases. Notably, all cases exhibited an mutant-type p53 expression pattern, and the Ki-67 proliferation index ranged from 5% to 80%. AcCC of the breast is a rare, triple-negative malignancy that typically presents as a BI-RADS 4 lesion in the upper outer quadrant. Its diagnosis is based on characteristic morphological features—primarily microglands and acinar patterns, along with less common cystic, follicular, clear cell, and solid architectures. This is supported by a distinctive immunohistochemical profile, which consistently includes mutant-type expression of p53 protein. A comprehensive understanding of the clinicopathological and immunophenotypic spectrum of AcCC is crucial for accurate diagnosis and differential diagnosis. Enhanced recognition of this entity, particularly its rare morphological variants, will help reduce diagnostic errors and guide more precise clinical management, ultimately improving prognostic assessment for affected patients.

title: Rare case of dual lesion: intraosseous microcystic meningioma – case report and review of literature
abstract_text: Abstract Introduction/background Intraosseous microcystic meningioma is an exceptionally rare clinical entity, representing a diagnostic challenge due to its atypical osteolytic presentation and specific histological features. This case is unique because it occurs in a 43-year-old patient—younger than the reported median age—and highlights specific MRI "shine-through" effects that can assist in preoperative differentiation from aggressive bone malignancies. Case presentation A 43-year-old woman presented with a six-month history of intermittent parietal pain. Imaging revealed a 1.9 × 0.9 cm osteolytic defect in the right frontal bone with internal septations. MRI showed T2-hyperintensity and heterogeneous enhancement, but no restricted diffusion on ADC maps. The patient underwent gross total resection with dural repair and titanium mesh reconstruction. Histopathology confirmed a WHO Grade I microcystic meningioma, positive for EMA, SSTR2, and D2-40. Conclusion The main "take-away" is that intraosseous microcystic meningioma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of solitary osteolytic skull lesions. Multi-parametric MRI, specifically the absence of restricted diffusion despite high DWI signal (T2 shine-through), is a key indicator of this benign, fluid-rich subtype.

title: Social media use duration and epigenetic aging among U.S. adults in the MIDUS refresher study
abstract_text: Social media platforms are central to daily social interaction, with emerging evidence linking higher engagement to adverse outcomes, including increased stress, sleep disturbance, and depressive symptoms. However, whether these digital exposures translate into measurable acceleration of biological aging remains unexplored, particularly among midlife and older adults. We analyzed cross-sectional data from 323 participants (Mean age = 47.5 years, SD = 11.8) in the Midlife in the United States Refresher Study who completed daily diary assessments of social media use duration and provided blood samples for epigenetic aging measurement. Epigenetic aging was quantified using DunedinPACE and GrimAge2 from genome-wide DNA methylation analysis. In a linear regression model controlling for differences in inter-assessment intervals, sociodemographic characteristics, health behaviors, and self-reported mental health, each additional hour of daily social media use was significantly associated with a 0.19-SD higher DunedinPACE score (95% CI: 0.08 to 0.29, p < 0.001). However, further adjustment for body mass index attenuated this association (0.09 SD increase, 95% CI: -0.01, 0.19, p = 0.088), suggesting that BMI may reflect the downstream consequences of broader behavioral, metabolic, psychosocial, environmental, and health-related processes relevant to the observed relationship. No associations were observed with GrimAge2 across any model. These findings provide preliminary evidence that social media use duration is associated with the pace of biological aging as measured by DunedinPACE. Future research should employ longitudinal designs with direct measurement of digital engagement, behavioral and psychosocial processes, and physiological mechanisms to clarify how digital environments may relate to biological aging over time.

title: Dynamic Organization of Narcissism-Related Psychological Processes During Everyday Social Interactions: A Preregistered Multilevel Investigation Across Two Intensive Longitudinal Datasets
abstract_text: This study examines whether individuals differ reliably in the dynamic organization of psychological processes that are theoretically related to narcissism during naturally occurring social interactions. Rather than treating narcissism as a single repeated state score, the study distinguishes agentic positive experience, superiority, shame, insecurity, anger, behavioral withdrawal, envy, resentment, and combative behavior. Across two intensive longitudinal datasets, we will estimate individual differences in average levels, volatility where distributionally appropriate, persistence across consecutive social interactions, reactivity to perceived status cues, and cross-lagged coupling among vulnerability-related, antagonistic, and grandiose processes. We will also test whether trait admiration and rivalry predict these dynamic parameters. Rationale Most research on narcissism in daily life focuses on between-person trait differences, average momentary levels, contemporaneous associations, or simple within-person variability. These approaches do not fully characterize how narcissism-related processes unfold over time. Two people with similar average levels may differ in whether their responses are stable or volatile, whether an activated state persists into the next interaction, whether they are especially reactive to admiration, criticism, exclusion, or status threat, and whether vulnerability-related experiences precede antagonistic or grandiose responses. The present study therefore conceptualizes dynamic organization as a multicomponent architecture comprising level, volatility, persistence, cue reactivity, and coupling among distinct processes. Primary research question Do individuals differ reliably in the dynamic organization of narcissism-related psychological processes during everyday social interactions, beyond differences in their average levels?

title: Percepción estudiantil y perfiles motivacionales ante la integración de Python en Probabilidad y Estadística
abstract_text: La enseñanza de la Probabilidad y Estadística (PyE) suele representar un desafío para muchos estudiantes, por lo que la motivación académica constituye un elemento relevante para favorecer el aprendizaje. En este contexto, la incorporación de lenguajes de programación ha sido propuesta como una estrategia que puede enriquecer el proceso formativo. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar, desde la perspectiva de la Teoría de la Autodeterminación, los tipos de motivación académica en estudiantes de ingeniería asociados al uso de Python como recurso de aprendizaje en PyE, así como las posibles diferencias según el sexo. La investigación adoptó un enfoque cuantitativo, con diseño no experimental, transversal y alcance descriptivo-comparativo. El estudio corresponde a un análisis secundario de datos derivados del proceso de validación de la Escala de Motivación Académica de Uso de Python en PyE (EMA-UPPyE). La muestra estuvo conformada por 76 estudiantes de segundo semestre (70 % hombres y 30 % mujeres), con una edad promedio de 19 años (DE = 1.56). Los resultados mostraron niveles altos de motivación intrínseca y extrínseca, así como niveles bajos de desmotivación. Además, se identificó una diferencia estadísticamente significativa en la dimensión de desmotivación (t(66.34) = 2.80, p = .007, d = 0.58), donde los hombres reportaron una media superior a la de las mujeres. En conjunto, los resultados sugieren una valoración favorable del uso de Python como recurso de aprendizaje en la asignatura de PyE y una percepción positiva de su utilidad académica y profesional entre los estudiantes participantes.

title: Pilot Study of Combined tDCS and Cognitive Training Intervention for Suicide Risk with Ecological Momentary Assessment: Feasibility and Acceptability in Psychiatric Inpatient Veterans
abstract_text: Objective: This pilot study examined the feasibility and acceptability of an impulsivity-targeted neuromodulation intervention and high-density ecological momentary assessment (EMA) in high-risk veterans with suicidal thoughts and behaviors following discharge from acute inpatient psychiatric care.Method: Fourteen adult veterans receiving acute psychiatric care screened for suicide risk were recruited to the study and completed a baseline assessment, 10 sessions of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) paired with cognitive training, one month of EMA surveys (2-3x per day) post-discharge, and questionnaires and cognitive tasks one- and two-months following the last intervention received.Results: Study feasibility was supported by a 21% enrollment rate, 56% intervention adherence, and no reported difficulties tolerating the intervention. Adherence to EMA surveys was high (77%) among participants who completed the EMA protocol, with the highest adherence in the first week followed by a reduction in subsequent weeks.Conclusions: This study demonstrated that neuromodulation and cognitive training interventions and high-density EMA designs are generally feasible and acceptable among veterans at high risk of suicide following acute psychiatric care. Recommendations for increasing feasibility and adherence to such interventions and suicide risk safety procedures for intensive EMA protocols with high-risk veterans are discussed.

title: Single-Scale EMA Latent Memory for Strictly Causal Dense Arm-Motion Recognition from Multi-Channel sEMG
abstract_text: Strictly causal dense arm-motion recognition from surface electromyography (sEMG) requires past context without future samples. We evaluated single-scale exponential moving average (EMA) latent memory as a lightweight causal temporal mechanism under a controlled, matched design. Causal CNN, causal CNN–Transformer (CT), and causal CNN with EMA memory (CEMA) were tested on a 30-subject, eight-channel, seven-class dataset in five subject-independent folds. At 300, 500, and 800 ms, five deterministic seeds were averaged within-fold before inference. CEMA accuracy exceeded CNN accuracy by 9.105, 9.313, and 9.657 percentage points, respectively (all Holm-adjusted paired-t p < 0.001). CEMA–CT differences were +0.209, −0.240, and −0.715 points, respectively; confidence intervals included zero, and directions varied across seeds. With parameters frozen, resetting memory at the current-window start reduced CEMA accuracy by 10.928–17.009 points. CEMA–CT B100 recall differences were −4.97, −12.84, and −16.54 points, respectively, whereas absolute-delay differences were 6.79, 7.71, and 6.94 ms, respectively, all below 8 ms. At 300 ms, CEMA used 6968 parameters and 0.751 M MACs, 48.0% fewer MACs than CT; CT required 2.31× CEMA’s full-buffer host-wall time. CEMA offers a favorable average accuracy–efficiency trade-off, although CT remains more responsive at transitions. Timing reflects full-buffer host inference only, not incremental, embedded, or end-to-end deployment.

title: Development of an LC-MS/MS Method for Simultaneous Quantification of Ibrutinib and Ritonavir in Plasma and Dried Plasma Spots
abstract_text: The instability of ibrutinib in plasma at room temperature necessitates temperature-controlled sample transport, complicating therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and multicenter studies. Dried plasma spots (DPSs) offer a potential advantage by enabling sample storage and transport under ambient conditions. The aim of this study was to develop and validate an LC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous quantification of ibrutinib and ritonavir in plasma and DPSs. Following validation of an extended plasma calibration range, DPS method development included card selection and subsequent validation in accordance with ICH M10 and EMA guidelines. The analytical method demonstrated robust performance in plasma for both analytes. For DPS sampling, ritonavir fulfilled all validation criteria. In contrast, ibrutinib showed significant instability in DPS samples at room temperature after 48 h and did not meet the predefined acceptance criteria under these conditions. Refrigerated storage improved stability within the acceptance criteria for at least one week. The developed method is suitable for simultaneous quantification of ibrutinib and ritonavir in plasma and for ritonavir in DPSs. While DPS sampling may offer logistical advantages, its successful application is dependent on analyte stability. For ibrutinib, the requirement for refrigerated storage limits the anticipated benefits, and further research is needed to optimize dried sampling strategies.

title: SR-JEPA: Learning Predictive Latent State in 3D Scenes
abstract_text: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting latent representations of missing observations, yet many masked JEPAs are evaluated primarily through the encoders they produce. We ask what a trained predictive pathway itself infers when an entire entity is absent from a native 3D scene. We introduce SR-JEPA, a point-native JEPA for scene-scale point clouds whose original frozen predictive pathway can be queried at a supplied location. At evaluation, every point of one object is removed before encoding and replaced by the same shape-free 32-point query at its centroid. Training uses only self-contained 3D EMA targets: no reconstruction, semantic labels, language, or lifted 2D features. On 5,953 held-out ARKitScenes objects, the imputed latent reaches 43.13% semantic-identity macro accuracy, 22.18 points above the strongest floor. Randomizing the prediction path removes 9.78 points, while substituting matched donor context removes 21.98 points. On 8,570 Sr3D support pairs, the full latent reaches 41.15 AP; identity decoded from the missing-object latent, combined with anchor identity and geometry, reaches 39.37 AP, leaving an unresolved 1.78-point residual. These results reveal a queryable, compositional 3D predictive state: the model completes context-dependent entity content, which downstream computation combines with metric geometry.

title: Deep Generalised Mixed Models: a Novel Neural Network Structure for Analysing Hierarchical Data
abstract_text: The experience sampling method (ESM) is a longitudinal research design where participants report their thoughts, emotional states and behaviours multiple times a day. Our work is motivated by such data collected by the GrowIt! app, which was released to investigate daily emotions among adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic. Current procedures to analyse ESM data face various challenges. While standard statistical techniques may not scale well to a high-dimensional setting, machine learning procedures can give biased results due to selection bias introduced by missingness. In our motivating dataset, adolescents dropped out due to previous strong feelings of negative emotions. Hence, the implied missing data are of the missing-at-random type that standard machine learning procedures cannot accommodate. We develop a novel neural network architecture that generalises mixed effects models to deep learning to overcome these challenges. It allows semi-parametric and flexible modelling of data's mean and correlation structure through fixed and random effects. For estimation, we use an adaptation of variational auto-encoders and a Bayesian data augmentation algorithm. Through this approach, the model can accommodate longitudinal outcomes following generic distributions, scale well to high-dimensional settings and provide valid inference when data are missing-at-random. We applied the Deep Generalised Mixed Model to the GrowIt! study and various simulations. The results show potential for the Deep Generalised Mixed Model, yet suboptimal performance due to model instability.

title: Environmental and Social Contexts Associated with Impulsivity and Alcohol Use Among Heavy Drinking College Students
abstract_text: Background: Although impulsivity is strongly linked to alcohol use, few studies have examined contextual factors that may impact impulsivity in real time. Thus, this study aimed to (1) determine which locations, social settings, and drinking contexts were associated with impulsivity and (2) examine whether the association between impulsivity and alcohol use in-the-moment was moderated by context. Methods: Participants were 89 (47 women) heavy drinking, college students who completed a 14-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA) study. Each day, participants completed three random reports, and two reports at the beginning and end of any drinking occasions. Results: At the between-person level, individuals who were more frequently at parties and received more drink offers reported higher than average impulsivity. At the within-person level, being at home, at work or school, or alone was associated with lower impulsivity whereas reporting a greater number of drinks consumed by others was associated with greater impulsivity. No context significantly impacted the association between impulsivity and alcohol use. Conclusions: Although certain contexts were associated with impulsivity, contexts did not heighten the risk for impulsivity and alcohol use in the moment. Additional research is needed to fully elucidate the associations between contextual factors and impulsivity in real time.

title: Deep Generalised Mixed Models: a Novel Neural Network Structure for Analysing Hierarchical Data
abstract_text: The experience sampling method (ESM) is a longitudinal research design where participants report their thoughts, emotional states and behaviours multiple times a day. Our work is motivated by such data collected by the GrowIt! app, which was released to investigate daily emotions among adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic. Current procedures to analyse ESM data face various challenges. While standard statistical techniques may not scale well to a high-dimensional setting, machine learning procedures can give biased results due to selection bias introduced by missingness. In our motivating dataset, adolescents dropped out due to previous strong feelings of negative emotions. Hence, the implied missing data are of the missing-at-random type that standard machine learning procedures cannot accommodate. We develop a novel neural network architecture that generalises mixed effects models to deep learning to overcome these challenges. It allows semi-parametric and flexible modelling of data's mean and correlation structure through fixed and random effects. For estimation, we use an adaptation of variational auto-encoders and a Bayesian data augmentation algorithm. Through this approach, the model can accommodate longitudinal outcomes following generic distributions, scale well to high-dimensional settings and provide valid inference when data are missing-at-random. We applied the Deep Generalised Mixed Model to the GrowIt! study and various simulations. The results show potential for the Deep Generalised Mixed Model, yet suboptimal performance due to model instability.

title: Motivation and affect across the menstrual cycle: a large scale ecological momentary assessment study.
abstract_text: This study investigates women’s self-reported changes in motivation, affective state and affective lability across the menstrual cycle. title: Pilot Study of Combined tDCS and Cognitive Training Intervention for Suicide Risk with Ecological Momentary Assessment: Feasibility and Acceptability in Psychiatric Inpatient Veterans
abstract_text: Objective: This pilot study examined the feasibility and acceptability of an impulsivity-targeted neuromodulation intervention and high-density ecological momentary assessment (EMA) in high-risk veterans with suicidal thoughts and behaviors following discharge from acute inpatient psychiatric care. Method: Fourteen adult veterans receiving acute psychiatric care screened for suicide risk were recruited to the study and completed a baseline assessment, 10 sessions of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) paired with cognitive training, one month of EMA surveys (2-3x per day) post-discharge, and questionnaires and cognitive tasks one- and two-months following the last intervention received. Results: Study feasibility was supported by a 21% enrollment rate, 56% intervention adherence, and no reported difficulties tolerating the intervention. Adherence to EMA surveys was high (77%) among participants who completed the EMA protocol, with the highest adherence in the first week followed by a reduction in subsequent weeks. Conclusions: This study demonstrated that neuromodulation and cognitive training interventions and high-density EMA designs are generally feasible and acceptable among veterans at high risk of suicide following acute psychiatric care. Recommendations for increasing feasibility and adherence to such interventions and suicide risk safety procedures for intensive EMA protocols with high-risk veterans are discussed.

title: Everyday smartphone language captures stable affective traits better than fluctuating states
abstract_text: Digital language is used to infer how people feel, from monitoring population well-being to assessing individual mental health, but how well it reflects subjective affective experience remains contested. We analyzed 3.45 million words of smartphone keyboard input from 410 adults followed for up to six months, paired with ecological momentary assessments and surveys. Prediction in private communication was strongest for trait negative affect, reaching a median r = .28, weaker for daily affective valence, r = .12, and negligible for momentary valence, r = .02. The same features predicted age strongly (r = .70), indicating that they captured meaningful person-level information. Prediction was higher in private than public communication, but this trait-level advantage was largely attenuated after matching text volume. Theory-guided associations were likewise clearer for stable between-person differences than for daily or momentary within-person fluctuations. Everyday smartphone language therefore appears better suited to capturing stable affective traits than to monitoring fluctuating states.

title: SR-JEPA: Learning Predictive Latent State in 3D Scenes
abstract_text: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting latent representations of missing observations, yet many masked JEPAs are evaluated primarily through the encoders they produce. We ask what a trained predictive pathway itself infers when an entire entity is absent from a native 3D scene. We introduce SR-JEPA, a point-native JEPA for scene-scale point clouds whose original frozen predictive pathway can be queried at a supplied location. At evaluation, every point of one object is removed before encoding and replaced by the same shape-free 32-point query at its centroid. Training uses only self-contained 3D EMA targets: no reconstruction, semantic labels, language, or lifted 2D features. On 5,953 held-out ARKitScenes objects, the imputed latent reaches 43.13% semantic-identity macro accuracy, 22.18 points above the strongest floor. Randomizing the prediction path removes 9.78 points, while substituting matched donor context removes 21.98 points. On 8,570 Sr3D support pairs, the full latent reaches 41.15 AP; identity decoded from the missing-object latent, combined with anchor identity and geometry, reaches 39.37 AP, leaving an unresolved 1.78-point residual. These results reveal a queryable, compositional 3D predictive state: the model completes context-dependent entity content, which downstream computation combines with metric geometry.
